chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a FreshBooks Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the client count, because it sets the FreshBooks plan. Lite covers 5 billable clients, Plus covers 50 and Premium is unlimited. A freelancer with 12 clients lands on Plus at $43 per month, or $516 per year, while Wave Starter, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja Pro list lower subscription prices for the same 12 clients.

Next, separate the subscription from the payment fees. FreshBooks, Wave, Square and the other tools that process payments each charge a percentage per card payment on top of the plan price. On a $2,000 invoice paid by card, 2.9% + $0.30 comes to $58.30, and 3.3% + $0.30 comes to $66.30. Bank transfers cost less: 1% of $2,000 is $20.

Then match the tool to the kind of record needed. Invoicing tools produce bills and track what clients owe. Accounting tools such as Zoho Books and Xero keep a full ledger with bank reconciliation. Bonsai sits closer to client management, with proposals, contracts and scheduling. For the ledger side, the [accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) roundup covers the bookkeeping options in more depth.

Run through these checks before comparing prices:

- How many clients are billed in a year, and does the count include archived clients?
- Will clients pay by card, bank transfer or both, and who absorbs the processing fee?
- Is a full ledger with bank reconciliation needed, or only invoices?
- How many people need a login, and is the seat price per user?
- Is payroll, mileage tracking or proposal software already paid for elsewhere? The [mileage tracker apps](/roundup/best-mileage-tracker-apps/) roundup lists dedicated options.

alternatives.heading: Wave Free Invoicing and Card Fees Compared with FreshBooks
alternatives.body:
Wave publishes a $0 Starter plan with unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records, plus a mobile app and a single dashboard for cash flow and customers. Pro costs $19 per month, or $190 billed annually, and adds automatic bank transaction import, automatic merging and categorizing of bank transactions, receipt capture and automated late payment reminders. Wave Advisors, a done-for-you bookkeeping service, starts at $149 per month.

Online payments are an option on either plan. Starter lists 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0.60 per American Express transaction. Pro lists 2.9% + $0 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0 per American Express transaction, with a footnote that the $0 fixed fee applies to the first 10 transactions per month.

A freelancer sending twelve $2,000 invoices a year that all clients pay by card shows the gap. On FreshBooks Plus, the subscription is $516 and card fees are 12 x $58.30 = $699.60, totaling $1,215.60. On Wave Starter, the subscription is $0 and card fees are 12 x $58.60 = $703.20. The yearly difference is $512.40, almost all of it the subscription.

Wave falls short of FreshBooks on project tools, since Wave's pricing page lists no time tracking or project profitability reports. Wave fits sole proprietors who mainly need invoices and bookkeeping.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Invoice Free Plan Versus FreshBooks Lite
alternatives.body:
Zoho Invoice is a free invoicing application from Zoho, described on its pricing page as a forever-free solution for small businesses. It creates tax-compliant invoices, emails them or saves them as PDF files, and sends automated payment reminders. Its pricing page also lists limits of 2 users, 3 projects and 500 invoices per year, plus "Powered by Zoho Invoice" branding. It also covers quotes, recurring invoices, expense categorizing, time and project logging, customizable templates and a self-service customer portal.

One Zoho Invoice account can hold up to two organizations. Zoho lists free email and voice support at 24/5. Zoho states that data for a user inactive for over 180 days is deleted in the following 20 days after notice, so a dormant account needs a login or a backup to keep its records. Zoho Invoice's pricing page lists no payment-processing price.

For a freelancer with 12 clients, FreshBooks Lite covers only 5, which pushes the account to Plus at $516 per year. Zoho Invoice costs $0 for the same 12 clients. Even a freelancer with 4 clients, who fits inside Lite, pays $276 per year ($23 x 12) on FreshBooks against $0 on Zoho Invoice.

Zoho Invoice falls short of FreshBooks on accounting depth: the Zoho Invoice page lists invoicing, expenses and time logging, while ledger reports sit in Zoho Books. Zoho Invoice fits people who need a no-cost billing tool and who add payment collection through a gateway of their choice.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Books Plans for Accounting and Invoices
alternatives.body:
Zoho Books is Zoho's accounting product. Its Free plan costs $0 per organization per month and stays available as long as annual revenue does not exceed $50,000. Free allows up to 1,000 invoices and 1,000 expenses a year and includes one user plus one accountant, email support, mileage tracking, bank reconciliation, recurring invoices and 50-plus reports.

Standard costs $20 per month, or $15 per month billed annually, and allows 3 users and up to 5,000 invoices a year. It adds bank feeds, progress invoicing, sales tax tracking and application programming interface (API) access. Professional costs $50 per month, or $40 billed annually, for 5 users with inventory tracking, multi-currency transactions, timesheet billing and project profitability. Zoho Books has a 14-day free trial.

A business with $80,000 in revenue is above the Free plan's $50,000 threshold. Standard billed annually costs $15 x 12 = $180 per year, and billed monthly costs $20 x 12 = $240. FreshBooks Plus for the same year costs $516, a difference of $336 against annual Zoho Books billing.

Zoho Books falls short of FreshBooks on simplicity, since a full accounting system carries more setup than an invoicing app. Zoho Books fits small businesses that want a ledger, bank feeds and reports at a lower subscription price than FreshBooks.

alternatives.heading: Xero Plans, Invoice Limits and Pricing
alternatives.body:
Xero sells three plans in the United States (US): Early at $27 per month, Growing at $59 and Established at $97. New customers receive 80% off for the first 3 months, which makes Early $5.40 per month at the start, and the regular price then applies and auto-renews monthly.

Early covers quotes, 20 invoices, 5 bills, bank reconciliation, Smart Document Capture, real-time reports, sales tax and a 30-day cash flow forecast. Growing removes the invoice and bill limits and adds a 60-day forecast, performance dashboards and budgets. Established adds multiple currencies, project time and cost tracking, employee expense and mileage claims and a 180-day forecast. Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, costs $36 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor on any plan.

A business that sends more than the 20 invoices listed for Early needs Growing. At $59 per month, that is $708 per year, compared with $516 on FreshBooks Plus, a difference of $192. Established at $97 per month costs $1,164 per year against $840 for FreshBooks Premium. FreshBooks payroll lists $40 per month plus $6 per user, so Xero's payroll add-on is $4 per month lower at the base.

Xero falls short of FreshBooks on price for small client lists, since FreshBooks Lite is $4 per month below Early. Xero fits businesses that want a full double-entry ledger and forecasting tools.

alternatives.heading: Invoice Ninja Free, Pro and Enterprise Pricing
alternatives.body:
Invoice Ninja offers a Free plan at $0 per month with 5 clients and unlimited invoices. It includes 11 invoice templates, logo branding, online payments, recurring invoices, product and inventory management, projects with billable time, vendors and expenses, a client portal and deposits or partial payments.

Ninja Pro costs $14 per month billed monthly, with a $28 saving on annual billing (two months free). Pro adds unlimited clients and invoices, removal of the Created by Invoice Ninja line, automated late-payment reminder emails, reports on invoices, expenses and profit and loss, and automatic US state sales tax calculation. Enterprise starts at $18 per month for 1 to 2 users and climbs to $300 per month for 51 to 100 users, with permissions per user, bank account sync and e-invoicing access. Premium Business is custom, from $280 per year.

A freelancer with 12 clients passes the Free plan's 5-client limit and needs Pro. Billed monthly, Pro costs $14 x 12 = $168 per year, and billed annually it costs $140. FreshBooks Plus costs $516 per year for the same 12 clients, so Pro lists $348 lower on monthly billing and $376 lower on annual billing.

Invoice Ninja falls short of FreshBooks on payroll, since its pricing page lists none. Invoice Ninja fits freelancers who want invoicing, time tracking and expenses at a flat low price.

alternatives.heading: Bonsai Per-User Plans for Freelancers and Teams
alternatives.body:
Bonsai charges per user per month. Billed annually, Basic costs $9, Essentials $19, Premium $29 and Elite $49, with Elite requiring at least 3 users. Billed monthly, the same plans cost $15, $25, $39 and $59. Basic covers time tracking, task management, a customer relationship tool and unlimited clients and projects.

Invoices and payments start at Essentials, which adds proposals and contracts, forms, scheduling, a client portal, and expense and income tracking. Premium adds project insights, workload management, a deals pipeline, profit and productivity reports, removal of Bonsai branding and integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, Zapier and Google. Elite adds custom permissions, timesheet locking and a custom data import.

For a two-person studio on Essentials, annual billing costs 2 x $19 x 12 = $456 per year and monthly billing costs 2 x $25 x 12 = $600. FreshBooks Plus with one Team Member add-on at $11 lists $54 per month, or $648 per year. On Premium, the same two people cost 2 x $29 x 12 = $696 billed annually.

Bonsai falls short of FreshBooks on accounting: its pricing page lists income and expense tracking but no double-entry ledger, and per-user pricing grows with every added person. Bonsai fits freelancers and small agencies that want proposals, contracts and invoices together.

alternatives.heading: Square Invoices and Card Processing Rates
alternatives.body:
Square Invoices belongs to Square's plan structure: Square Free costs $0 per month per location, Plus costs $49 and Premium costs $149. Card payments made online or through an invoice cost 3.3% + $0.30 on Free and 2.9% + $0.30 on Plus and Premium. ACH bank transfers through an invoice cost 1% with a $1 minimum, capped at $10 on Plus and Premium. Manual card entry costs 3.5% + $0.15.

Square's invoice features include unlimited invoices, recurring invoices on daily, weekly, monthly or yearly schedules, batch invoices to multiple customers, milestone payment schedules, estimates that convert to invoices and reporting on what is paid, unpaid and overdue.

On a $2,000 invoice paid by card, Square Free charges $66.30 and Plus charges $58.30, matching FreshBooks' 2.9% + $0.30 at $58.30. Square Plus saves 0.4 percentage points on card volume, so $49 per month is recovered at $12,250 of monthly card volume. A $2,000 invoice paid by bank transfer costs $20 on Square Free and $10 on Plus after the cap, against 1%, or $20, on FreshBooks.

Square falls short of FreshBooks on accounting and expense features, since Square's pricing page focuses on selling and payments. Square fits sellers who invoice by card and bank transfer and also take in-person sales.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Several bookkeeping jobs call for a different category of product:

- Bookkeeping done by a person is covered in the [bookkeeping services for small businesses](/roundup/best-bookkeeping-services-for-small-businesses/) comparison; Wave Advisors is the only listed service here, starting at $149 per month.
- QuickBooks is covered on its own page, the [QuickBooks alternatives comparison](/alternatives/quickbooks/).
- FreshBooks Select pricing is quote-based, so a Select-level comparison needs a consultant quote that this page cannot show.
- Business checking accounts and cards sit outside these tools; see the [business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/).

If the question is which accounting tools suit self-employed filers, read the [accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) roundup.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on FreshBooks Alternatives
alternatives.body:
A pricing or limit change could shift which option costs least for the same client list:

- FreshBooks changing the 5, 50 and unlimited client limits on Lite, Plus and Premium, or its $23, $43 and $70 monthly prices.
- Wave extending Pro's 2.9% + $0 card rate beyond the first 10 transactions per month.
- Zoho Books moving the $50,000 revenue threshold on its Free plan.
- Xero raising or removing the 20-invoice limit on Early.
- Bonsai or Invoice Ninja changing per-user pricing or the 5-client Free limit.
- Square Plus changing its $49 monthly location fee or the 2.9% + $0.30 invoice card rate.

For businesses comparing paid plans, include card volume alongside the monthly price, since a 0.4 percentage point card-fee gap is worth $8 on a $2,000 invoice. Browse the [financial product comparison hub](/compare/) for other fee breakdowns.

stillBetterFit.heading: When FreshBooks Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
FreshBooks keeps invoices, estimates, proposals, expenses, mileage and time tracking in one subscription. Plus includes proposals and client retainers, and Premium removes the client limit entirely. A freelancer who bills by the hour, tracks time against projects and wants one login for the whole workflow gets all of that at $43 per month on Plus.

FreshBooks accepts credit and debit cards, ACH bank transfers, Apple Pay, Google Pay and buy now, pay later options. Its card rate of 2.9% + $0.30 matches Square Plus and its 1% ACH rate matches Square's.

The pricing page also lists a 30-day free trial and a limited-time 80% discount for the first 4 months, which puts Lite at $4.60 per month and Plus at $8.60 at the start. With that discount, a first year on Lite totals $202.40 ($18.40 + 8 x $23), and the client limit of the chosen plan decides whether a second billing tool is needed.

verdict:
Wave, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja Free publish $0 subscription tiers, Zoho Books and Xero add full accounting at $15 to $97 per month, Bonsai prices by user, and Square prices by payment method. FreshBooks sits above most of them on subscription price, with client limits that set the plan.

To compare FreshBooks alternatives for your own invoicing, write down the number of billable clients, the share of payments by card, the number of people who need a login and whether a full ledger is required, then apply the matching prices in the table.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of FreshBooks?
faqs.answer: Wave, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja publish $0 plans for invoicing. Zoho Books and Xero add full accounting, starting at $0 and $27 per month. Bonsai prices per user and bundles proposals and contracts, while Square Invoices prices by payment method. FreshBooks lists Lite at $23, Plus at $43 and Premium at $70 per month.

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to FreshBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wave Starter costs $0 with unlimited invoices and estimates, Zoho Invoice is listed as forever free, Invoice Ninja Free allows 5 clients, and Zoho Books Free applies while annual revenue stays under $50,000 with up to 1,000 invoices a year.

faqs.question: How do FreshBooks card fees compare with Wave and Square?
faqs.answer: FreshBooks Payments charges 2.9% + $0.30 per credit card transaction, which is $58.30 on a $2,000 invoice. Wave Starter charges 2.9% + $0.60 ($58.60). Square charges 3.3% + $0.30 on Free ($66.30) and 2.9% + $0.30 on Plus and Premium ($58.30). FreshBooks and Square both list 1% for bank transfers.

faqs.question: Which FreshBooks alternative has no client limit?
faqs.answer: Invoice Ninja Pro, at $14 per month billed monthly, lists unlimited clients and invoices, and Bonsai Basic lists unlimited clients. Wave Starter lists unlimited invoices. FreshBooks limits Lite to 5 clients and Plus to 50, with Premium unlimited at $70 per month.

faqs.question: Do FreshBooks alternatives include payroll?
faqs.answer: Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, is an add-on at $36 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor. FreshBooks Payroll is $40 per month plus $6 per user. Wave, Zoho Invoice, Invoice Ninja and Bonsai list no payroll product on their pricing pages.

title: Wealthfront Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Plans Compared
h1: Wealthfront Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Plans Compared
metaDescription: Compare Wealthfront alternatives for 2026: Betterment, Schwab, Vanguard, Fidelity Go, Ally, Acorns, and M1 with published fees, minimums, and cash rates.
intro: Betterment, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, Vanguard Digital Advisor, Fidelity Go, Ally Invest Robo Portfolios, Acorns, and M1 are seven Wealthfront alternatives that provide automated investing or portfolio tools with published advisory fees from $0 up to 0.65% annually (Betterment Premium), alongside flat monthly subscriptions. The choice depends on whether an account requires tax-loss harvesting, human coaching, zero advisory fees, or a cash reserve with an annual percentage yield (APY). The table lists each service's published advisory fee, account minimum and cash features as of November 17, 2026. [Wealthfront](https://www.wealthfront.com/) charges an annual advisory fee of 0.25% on its automated Wealthfront Portfolio, with no advisory fee on its self-directed Brokerage Account where clients can trade an exchange-traded fund (ETF) or individual stock. Wealthfront lists personal, joint, and trust taxable accounts, Traditional, Roth, and SEP retirement accounts, and 529 Education Savings Accounts. Its Cash Account lists up to a 4.45% APY (a base 3.55% APY as of November 13, 2026, plus an APY Boost up to a $150,000 balance) with zero account fees and up to $8M in FDIC insurance eligibility through program banks. Fees and prices across all providers are as published on each provider's site on November 17, 2026 and can change over time.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Wealthfront Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting a Wealthfront alternative starts with comparing percentage advisory fees against flat monthly charges. Wealthfront charges 0.25% per year, which amounts to $25 annually on a $10,000 balance. In contrast, flat fees take a fixed dollar amount regardless of portfolio growth: Acorns charges $4, $8, or $12 per month, while M1 charges a $3 monthly platform fee that is waived once platform assets exceed $10,000. On small accounts, a fixed $5 monthly fee equals $60 per year, which is 0.60% of a $10,000 account, whereas a percentage fee remains proportionate to the balance.

Account minimums also determine which services can be opened immediately. Wealthfront requires $1 to start a self-directed Brokerage Account, while Vanguard Digital Advisor requires $100 to enroll. Ally Invest Robo Portfolios also sets a $100 minimum. Fidelity Go requires $0 to open and $10 to begin investing. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios sets a higher entry threshold, requiring a $5,000 minimum balance to open an account.

Tax-loss harvesting rules vary widely across automated platforms. Wealthfront provides tax-loss harvesting across its taxable portfolios and publishes a claim that tax-loss harvesting can typically cover the annual fee more than 4.2 times over for Classic portfolio clients. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios offers tax-loss harvesting with no added advisory fee, but only for enrolled taxable accounts with at least $50,000. Fidelity Go reserves tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts with $25,000 or more invested in stock-holding Flex Funds.

Cash management features differ in yield and structure. Wealthfront provides up to 4.45% APY through program banks with up to $8M in FDIC insurance eligibility. Betterment lists a Cash Reserve at a variable 3.50% base APY as of September 21, 2026, with an optional 0.75% boost for qualifying new clients up to $1M. M1 lists a High-Yield Cash Account at 3.35% APY with a $100 initial deposit. Ally Invest Robo Portfolios holds a 30% cash buffer earning 3.20% monthly interest in its cash-enhanced portfolio, though Ally notes that cash buffer is not FDIC insured.

For related reading, see [Compare Financial Products](/compare/) and the [Robinhood alternatives](/alternatives/robinhood/) page.

alternatives.heading: Betterment Pricing Among Wealthfront Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Betterment provides automated investing portfolios, tax-loss harvesting, a self-directed brokerage trading stocks and ETFs with no commission fees, and a Cash Reserve account. Betterment charges $5 per month for investing balances under $24,000, but reduces the fee to 0.25% annually if the client sets up monthly recurring deposits of $200 or more, or when the balance reaches $24,000. Balances between $1 million and $2 million pay a discounted 0.15% on that portion, and assets above $2 million pay 0.10%. Betterment also offers a Premium plan at a 0.65% annual fee that includes advisor access and requires $100,000 in eligible investments. Betterment waives wrap fees on self-directed assets.

Cash Reserve pays a variable base APY of 3.50% as of September 21, 2026, with a $10 minimum deposit, plus a 0.75% APY boost up to $1M for new clients through February 15, 2027, with up to $8M in joint FDIC insurance. Betterment checking has no foreign transaction or ATM withdrawal fees.

On a $10,000 balance without recurring deposits, Betterment costs $5 per month, totaling $60 per year. Wealthfront charges 0.25% on that same $10,000, which is $25 per year, making Wealthfront $35 cheaper. With $200 monthly recurring deposits, Betterment charges 0.25%, matching Wealthfront's $25 cost.

Betterment falls short of Wealthfront for investors with small balances who do not maintain a recurring deposit of $200, because the $5 monthly fee equals a higher percentage. Betterment fits investors who can deposit $200 each month or who hold more than $1 million to qualify for progressive tiered fee discounts.

alternatives.heading: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios Among Zero-Fee Wealthfront Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Schwab Intelligent Portfolios is an automated investment advisory service that charges no advisory fee and no commissions. Investors still pay the underlying operating expenses of the ETFs held in the portfolio. Schwab notes that it earns revenue from other sources, including Schwab ETFs management fees and cash allocation.

To open an account, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios requires a minimum investment of $5,000. Automated tax-loss harvesting is available at no extra fee, but clients must enroll and maintain at least $50,000 in a taxable portfolio.

On a $10,000 portfolio, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges $0 in advisory fees. Wealthfront charges 0.25%, which totals $25 per year. On a $50,000 portfolio, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios still charges $0 in advisory fees and activates tax-loss harvesting, whereas Wealthfront charges 0.25%, totaling $125 per year.

Schwab Intelligent Portfolios falls short of Wealthfront on account accessibility and lower-balance tax management. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios fits investors who have at least $5,000 to invest and want automated ETF management without paying an advisory fee.

alternatives.heading: Vanguard Digital Advisor Portfolios and Asset Costs
alternatives.body:
Vanguard Digital Advisor is an automated portfolio management service that builds portfolios using Vanguard ETFs. Vanguard Digital Advisor charges a $0 advisory fee for the first 90 days, though underlying ETF investment costs apply throughout. After the promotional period, Vanguard states an all-index portfolio costs about $15 to $16 per year for every $10,000 managed. For an active and index mix, the net advisory and fund cost is no more than $20 per $10,000 annually.

Vanguard Digital Advisor requires $100 in assets to enroll. Portfolio options include an all-index strategy, an active and index mix, and an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) allocation.

On a $10,000 balance in an all-index strategy, Vanguard Digital Advisor costs roughly $15 to $16 annually. Wealthfront's 0.25% advisory fee equals $25 per year before underlying ETF expenses.

 Vanguard Digital Advisor fits investors who want low-cost index-based portfolio management from Vanguard with a low $100 entry requirement.

alternatives.heading: Fidelity Go Advisory Tiers and Coaching
alternatives.body:
Fidelity Go is an automated robo-advisor that scales advisory fees based on account size. Accounts with balances under $25,000 pay a $0 annual advisory fee. Accounts with $25,000 or more pay an annual advisory fee of 0.35%. There is no minimum balance required to open an account, though the balance must reach at least $10 before Fidelity Go invests the funds.

Clients with $25,000 or more receive unlimited one-on-one financial coaching sessions and automated tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts invested in Fidelity Flex Funds that hold stocks. Fidelity Go provides financial planning tools to all customers regardless of balance.

On a $20,000 balance, Fidelity Go charges $0 in advisory fees. Wealthfront charges 0.25%, which totals $50 per year on $20,000. However, on a $30,000 balance, Fidelity Go's 0.35% fee equals $105 annually, whereas Wealthfront's 0.25% fee equals $75 annually, making Wealthfront $30 less expensive.

Fidelity Go falls short of Wealthfront on pricing once an account passes $25,000, charging 0.35% compared with Wealthfront's 0.25%. Fidelity Go fits investors with balances below $25,000 seeking free portfolio management, or those above $25,000 who want one-on-one financial coaching.

alternatives.heading: Ally Invest Robo Portfolios and Cash Buffers
alternatives.body:
Ally Invest Robo Portfolios offers two automated portfolio options with a $100 opening minimum. The cash-enhanced portfolio allocates roughly 30% of assets to an interest-earning cash buffer and charges no advisory fee. The market-focused portfolio keeps approximately 98% invested with roughly 2% cash and charges an annual advisory fee of 0.30%, which equates to $3 per $1,000 managed.

Both options provide fee-free portfolio rebalancing. The cash buffer earns 3.20% interest credited monthly, though Ally notes that the cash buffer inside the robo portfolio is not FDIC insured. For self-directed accounts, Ally offers a cash brokerage account with no minimum and a margin account with a $2,000 minimum. Ally also lists Personal Advice for accounts with at least $100,000.

On a $10,000 investment in Ally's market-focused portfolio, the 0.30% advisory fee equals $30 per year. Wealthfront's 0.25% fee equals $25 per year, saving $5 annually compared with Ally. In Ally's cash-enhanced portfolio, the advisory fee is $0, but $3,000 of a $10,000 balance remains uninvested in cash.

Ally Invest Robo Portfolios falls short of Wealthfront because its invested portfolio carries a higher 0.30% fee, and its cash-enhanced portfolio holds 30% out of the market without FDIC coverage. Ally Invest Robo Portfolios fits investors who want automated rebalancing with a built-in interest-bearing cash reserve.

alternatives.heading: Acorns Subscription Plans and Spare Change Roundups
alternatives.body:
Acorns operates on a tiered subscription pricing model rather than an asset-based percentage fee. The Bronze plan costs $4 per month, Silver costs $8 per month, and Gold costs $12 per month. Acorns' pricing page lists a $10,000 life insurance policy and a will among its Gold-plan benefits.

Core features include round-up investing of spare change. Silver and Gold tiers add the Acorns Later retirement account, offering a 1% match on new IRA contributions in the first year on Silver and a 3% match on Gold. Acorns provides an Emergency Savings account with a 3.59% variable APY as of September 22, 2026. Gold adds Early Invest, an investment account for children with a 1% match.

Acorns charges $48 annually on Bronze ($4 x 12), $96 annually on Silver ($8 x 12), and $144 annually on Gold ($12 x 12). On a $5,000 balance, Bronze at $48 per year represents an effective 0.96% fee, whereas Wealthfront's 0.25% fee equals $12.50. On a $50,000 balance, Acorns Bronze costs $48 per year (roughly 0.10%), while Wealthfront charges $125 per year.

 Acorns fits micro-investors who want automated spare-change roundups and retirement account matching incentives.

alternatives.heading: M1 Platform Fees and Self-Directed Brokerage
alternatives.body:
M1 charges no commission, trading, or management fees for its self-directed brokerage. It applies a $3 monthly platform fee, which is waived for clients who hold more than $10,000 in platform assets.

M1 provides a High-Yield Cash Account offering a 3.35% APY with a $100 initial deposit required to earn the stated yield. M1 also offers margin loans at 5.90% for accounts holding $2,000 or more in eligible securities. Account balances are protected by SIPC up to $500,000, which includes up to $250,000 for cash claims.

For an investor with an $8,000 balance, M1's $3 monthly fee totals $36 per year ($3 x 12), which represents an effective 0.45% fee. Wealthfront's 0.25% fee on $8,000 is $20 per year. Once an investor holds $12,000 on M1, the platform fee drops to $0, while Wealthfront charges $30 annually.

 M1 fits self-directed investors who hold more than $10,000 to avoid platform fees.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body: investors who want to pick individual stocks or need personalized tax or legal guidance, since this page lists automated-investing fees only. Wealthfront charges a 0.25% annual fee on automated portfolios, while services like Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charge no advisory fee.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer
alternatives.body: Several pricing moves could shift the comparative cost among Wealthfront alternatives. If Wealthfront adjusted its 0.25% advisory fee or altered its Cash Account APY structure, the cost gap against zero-fee options would shift. If Schwab Intelligent Portfolios lowered its $5,000 entry minimum or its $50,000 tax-loss harvesting requirement, it would become accessible to smaller taxable accounts. If Betterment removed its $5 monthly charge for accounts under $24,000 that lack recurring deposits, it would match Wealthfront at lower balances. If Fidelity Go changed its $25,000 threshold for free advisory services, smaller balances would face different fee calculations.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Wealthfront Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Wealthfront fits investors who want completely automated portfolio management paired with integrated cash and borrowing features. Its 0.25% annual advisory fee covers personalized risk-adjusted portfolios, automatic rebalancing, and tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts. Wealthfront publishes an example showing that a $15,000 balance incurs an estimated monthly cost of $3.18 at 0.25%. Wealthfront also claims that its tax-loss harvesting typically covers the annual advisory fee more than 4.2 times over for Classic portfolio clients.

Beyond automated core portfolios, Wealthfront offers direct indexing and specialized products like a Bond Ladder. Its self-directed Brokerage Account allows clients to buy stocks and ETFs with a $1 starting minimum and zero advisory fees. For cash management, the Wealthfront Cash Account offers up to 4.45% APY (with a base APY of 3.55% as of November 13, 2026, plus an APY Boost up to a $150,000 balance) with zero account fees, free 24/7 instant withdrawals, and up to $8M in FDIC insurance eligibility through program banks.

Investors who want taxable accounts, retirement IRAs, and 529 college savings accounts in one system find Wealthfront well matched.

verdict: Choosing among Wealthfront alternatives comes down to fee structures, minimum deposit requirements, and portfolio management preferences. Betterment and Fidelity Go offer percentage-based fees or fee waivers on specific balances, while Schwab Intelligent Portfolios and Vanguard Digital Advisor reduce or eliminate advisory fees for accounts meeting their entry thresholds. Acorns and M1 use flat subscription models that benefit specific balance tiers. The table above lists each service's published advisory fee, account minimum and plan fees as of November 17, 2026.

faqs.question: What are the top alternatives to Wealthfront?
faqs.answer: Betterment, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, Vanguard Digital Advisor, Fidelity Go, Ally Invest Robo Portfolios, Acorns, and M1 are seven prominent alternatives offering automated portfolios, flat subscription pricing, or self-directed investing.

faqs.question: Which Wealthfront alternative has no advisory fee?
faqs.answer: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges a $0 advisory fee on portfolios with at least $5,000. Fidelity Go charges $0 in advisory fees on balances under $25,000. Ally Invest Robo Portfolios charges no advisory fee on its cash-enhanced portfolio with a 30% cash buffer. Vanguard Digital Advisor charges a $0 advisory fee for the first 90 days.

faqs.question: Do Wealthfront alternatives offer tax-loss harvesting?
faqs.answer: Yes, but requirements vary. Betterment features tax-loss harvesting on automated taxable accounts. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios offers tax-loss harvesting at no extra fee for enrolled taxable accounts of $50,000 or more. Fidelity Go provides tax-loss harvesting on taxable accounts with $25,000 or more holding stock Flex Funds.

faqs.question: What is the minimum deposit to open a Wealthfront alternative?
faqs.answer: Minimums range from $0 to $5,000. Fidelity Go requires $0 to open and $10 to invest. Betterment has no minimum balance. Vanguard Digital Advisor and Ally Invest Robo Portfolios require $100. M1 requires $100 for its High-Yield Cash Account stated APY, and Schwab Intelligent Portfolios requires $5,000.

faqs.question: Are advisory fees the only cost with robo-advisors?
faqs.answer: No, advisory fees do not cover ETF operating expenses. Investors across all platforms, including Wealthfront and its alternatives, pay the underlying expense ratios of the ETFs held in their portfolios. Some services also charge flat platform fees, such as M1's $3 monthly fee on balances under $10,000.

title: Monarch Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices Compared
h1: Monarch Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices Compared
metaDescription: Compare Monarch Money alternatives: YNAB, Copilot Money, Quicken Simplifi, PocketGuard, Tiller and Goodbudget, with regular plan prices and trials.
intro:
YNAB, Copilot Money, Quicken Simplifi, PocketGuard, Tiller and Goodbudget are six Monarch Money alternatives, with regular entry prices ranging from a $0 free plan to $109 per year. [Monarch Money](https://www.monarchmoney.com/pricing) sells two subscription tiers: Core at $99.99 per year or $14.99 per month, and Plus at $199.99 per year. Monarch Money lists a free first week under the phrase "Your first week is on us" and provides a no-questions-asked money-back guarantee with permission to cancel anytime. Monarch Money notes that it displays no ads, states that it never sells financial data, and maintains a 4.9 rating across more than 100,000 reviews as stated on its pricing page. Monarch Money recommends completing sign-up on the web rather than through the Apple App Store or Google Play.

For readers who want a broader overview of personal finance software, our [best budgeting apps roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps/) tracks wider category options. Partners managing money together can examine the [best budgeting apps for couples roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps-for-couples/), and planners establishing spending categories can review our [guide on how to make a budget](/guides/how-to-make-a-budget/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Monarch Money Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting a replacement for Monarch Money begins with five operational factors: the billing commitment, the length of the evaluation trial, the method of connecting financial accounts, the underlying budgeting model, and whether an application interface or a spreadsheet fits daily tracking habits.

First, assess the billing commitment. Monarch Money Core charges $99.99 on an annual basis or $14.99 on a month-to-month schedule. Paying month to month for 12 months totals $179.88, which is an $79.89 premium over the single annual payment. YNAB charges $109 annually or $14.99 monthly, yielding the same $179.88 annual total on monthly billing. PocketGuard offers an annual tier at $74.99, a monthly rate at $12.99 (which totals $155.88 over 12 months), and a permanent Lifetime purchase at $149.99. Tiller avoids monthly subscriptions entirely by charging $99 per year. Goodbudget provides a $0 tier alongside an $80 annual plan or a $10 monthly rate ($120 per year).

Second, evaluate the free trial terms. Monarch Money lists a 7-day free trial under the phrase "Your first week is on us." PocketGuard also uses a 7-day trial across its plans. In contrast, YNAB offers a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card details at registration, meaning no charge occurs unless the user chooses to subscribe. Tiller grants a 30-day trial without charging the card until the period concludes, paired with a subsequent 30-day refund window that offers up to 60 days of risk-free evaluation. Copilot Money and Quicken Simplifi list no specific free trial days on their pricing pages.

Third, review bank connectivity and platforms. Quicken Simplifi connects to 14,000+ financial institutions, while Copilot Money connects to 16,000+ banks. Tiller pulls transaction data automatically into personal spreadsheets. Goodbudget restricts automatic bank synchronization to United States (US) banks on its Premium tier. Copilot Money supports iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Web, whereas Goodbudget supports Web, Android, and iPhone.

Fourth, determine the budgeting methodology. Monarch Money offers general expense categorizing, forecasting, and investment monitoring. Users can test zero-allocation math using our [zero-based budget calculator](/budget/zero-based-budget-calculator/). Quicken Simplifi organizes spending through a custom Spending Plan and projects cash flow 12 months into the future. Goodbudget enforces digital envelope budgeting, allocating specific balances to fixed categories.

Finally, decide between a standalone application and a spreadsheet. Applications like Copilot Money and Goodbudget provide mobile app interfaces.

alternatives.heading: Goodbudget Envelope Budgeting and Free Tier Versus Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
Goodbudget is an envelope budgeting platform available on the Web, Android, and iPhone. Its pricing page features a Free plan at $0 that includes 10 regular envelopes, 10 more envelopes, 1 account, 2 devices, 1 year of historical records, debt tracking, and community support. Goodbudget Premium costs $10 per month or $80 per year, expanding features to automatic bank synchronization for US institutions, unlimited envelopes, unlimited accounts, 5 devices, 7 years of transaction history, and direct email support.

Goodbudget fits planners who want envelope budgeting and who prefer starting on a $0 plan before paying for software.

Goodbudget falls short of Monarch Money in comprehensive asset tracking and modern account synchronization. Goodbudget Free restricts users to a single account and omits automatic bank sync. Even Goodbudget Premium limits automated sync to US banks and omits deeper investment tracking, forecasting tools, and small business revenue tracking.

Comparing financial plans, Goodbudget Free costs $0, providing an annual savings of $99.99 compared to Monarch Money Core and $199.99 compared to Monarch Money Plus. Goodbudget Premium at $80 per year billed annually saves $19.99 per year relative to Monarch Money Core. On monthly schedules, Goodbudget Premium at $10 per month costs $120.00 annually, which is $59.88 less than Monarch Money Core's $179.88 annual total on monthly billing.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
- People who require completely offline bookkeeping with paper receipts or locally hosted desktop files.
- Businesses needing specialized enterprise payroll, double-entry ledgers, and formal client invoicing.
- Anyone who does not want to connect banking credentials or manually record personal transactions.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer
alternatives.body:
- Monarch Money altering its $99.99 Core or $199.99 Plus prices, or eliminating its 7-day trial.
- YNAB shifting its 34-day no-card trial policy or adjusting its $109 annual list price.
- Copilot Money publishing a permanent monthly plan price or officially launching its multi-user household system.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Monarch Money Is Still the Better Fit

These capabilities sit beyond envelope tools like Goodbudget or subscriptions like YNAB. Monarch Money accommodates users who prefer flexibility by supporting monthly billing at $14.99 alongside its $99.99 annual Core rate. New subscribers receive a free first week under the "Your first week is on us" trial and access to a no-questions-asked money-back guarantee.

verdict:
Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year, while alternatives range from Goodbudget's $0 Free tier to YNAB and Copilot Money at $109 per year. Quicken Simplifi offers a lower annual regular list price of about $83.88 ($6.99 per month), PocketGuard provides budgeters an annual rate of $74.99 and a permanent Lifetime purchase at $149.99, and Tiller matches Monarch Money almost dollar for dollar at $99 per year for automated spreadsheet feeds.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Mercury Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting an alternative to Mercury requires evaluating fee structures, interest requirements, branch access, multi-currency handling, and team expense controls.

First, assess transaction and wire charges. Mercury charges $0 for domestic wires and USD international wires, while charging a 1% currency exchange fee on non-USD international wires. Wise Business charges a fixed $6.11 fee to receive domestic wires and sends wire transfers starting at $1.13. Chase Business Complete Banking charges a $15 monthly service fee (unless waived) and limits teller transactions, while Performance Business Checking at $40 per month includes incoming wires and your two most expensive outgoing domestic wires.

Second, compare yields on idle cash balances. Mercury Treasury offers up to a 4.42% yield through the JPMorgan U.S. Treasury Plus Money Market Fund, but restricts eligibility to accounts holding $250,000 or more. If your balance sits below that threshold, Relay provides 1.19% APY on Starter ($0 per month), 1.87% APY on Grow ($30 per month), and 3.21% APY on Scale ($90 per month). Bluevine Standard offers 1.3% APY if you meet a monthly activity goal, Plus offers 1.75% APY up to $250,000 for $30 per month, and Premier offers 3.3% APY for $95 per month. Lili offers variable savings yields of 2.25% APY up to $500,000 and 4.00% APY from $500,000 to $1,000,000, while Novo Savings requires a minimum balance of $50,000 to earn 2% APY.

Third, verify account structure and team delegation. Relay allows up to 20 individual checking accounts on Starter and up to 50 on Scale, with 50 debit and credit cards across all tiers. Brex organizes corporate spend across teams, charging $0 per user on Essentials and $12 per user per month on Premium for custom expense review chains and live budgets. Mercury includes virtual and physical cards with spend limits and duplicate subscription detection.

Run through these five practical checks before switching providers:

- Does the business deposit physical cash or require teller services at a branch?
- Does the company send domestic or foreign currency wires every month?
- What is your average operating balance, and does it meet minimum interest thresholds?
- How many distinct checking accounts does your bookkeeping system require?
- How many employees need corporate cards or custom payment approvals?

alternatives.heading: Relay Multi-Account Checking and Tiered Savings Rates
alternatives.body:
Relay is a financial technology company that provides banking services through Thread Bank, Member FDIC. Relay imposes no minimum balance requirements, no hidden fees, and no overdraft charges. Every plan includes 50 credit and debit cards, invoice creation and tracking, accounting integrations with QuickBooks and Xero, and unlimited user seats.

Relay structures its service across three tiers. Relay Starter costs $0 per month and includes 20 individual checking accounts per business, a 1.19% APY on savings, 1% cash back on credit cards, built-in spend controls, and receipt upload reminders. Relay Grow costs $30 per month ($360 per year) and includes a 14-day trial, raising yields to 1.87% APY on savings and 1.25% cash back, while adding multi-step approval rules, recurring invoices, bookkeeping automations, and batch vendor payments. Relay Scale costs $90 per month under a limited-time discount from $120 ($1,080 per year), providing 50 checking accounts, 3.21% APY on savings, 1.5% cash back, $0 same-day ACH, cash flow insights, and phone support. Rates were accurate as of September 17, 2026, and remain variable.

A business holding $100,000 in savings demonstrates the arithmetic across Relay tiers. On Relay Starter at 1.19% APY, the annual yield is $1,190 with $0 in software fees. On Relay Scale at 3.21% APY, the annual interest generated is $3,210. Subtracting the $1,080 annual plan fee ($90 multiplied by 12) yields $2,130 in net earnings. That results in $940 more than Starter ($2,130 minus $1,190).

Relay fits businesses that separate funds across multiple checking accounts and desire cash back with savings interest. Versus Mercury, Relay Starter caps checking accounts at 20, whereas Mercury provides checking and savings with $0 domestic wires. Relay Scale requires a $90 monthly fee to eliminate same-day ACH fees, which Mercury includes on its $0 core plan.

alternatives.heading: Novo Digital Checking and ATM Fee Reimbursements
alternatives.body:
Novo is a fintech company that partners with Middlesex Federal Savings, F.A., Member FDIC, to provide banking services. Novo states that it is trusted by over 250,000 small businesses. Novo charges no monthly fees, requires no minimum balance, and claims no transaction limits. Novo charges no fee to open an account, charges no ATM fees, and reimburses third-party ATM fees up to $7 per month across domestic and international machines at month end.

Novo includes free standard ACH transfers and accepts incoming domestic and international wires at no cost. Accounts feature FDIC insurance up to $5,000,000 per depositor through its partner bank sweep network. Novo Business Checking does not earn interest. Novo Savings pays a 2% APY, but only after an account reaches a balance of $50,000 or more. Novo combines checking, payments, invoicing, bookkeeping, and payroll connections in one interface.

For a business with a $50,000 reserve, Novo Savings earns 2% APY, producing $1,000 in annual interest with zero account fees. On an account balance of $40,000, Novo Savings yields $0 in interest because it does not meet the $50,000 minimum threshold.

Novo fits small businesses seeking straightforward checking with ATM reimbursements. Versus Mercury, Novo does not offer an equivalent to Mercury Treasury for balances over $250,000.

alternatives.heading: Bluevine Interest Checking and Embedded Credit Lines
alternatives.body:
Bluevine is a financial technology company with deposits FDIC insured through Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC, and program banks, providing protection up to $3,000,000. Bluevine Standard charges $0 per month, with no overdraft fees, no minimum balance requirements, and free standard ACH transfers.

Bluevine Standard pays a 1.3% APY on checking balances if the account meets a monthly activity goal. Bluevine Plus costs $30 per month and pays 1.75% APY up to $250,000. Bluevine Premier costs $95 per month and pays 3.3% APY on all balances. Both tiers also carry fee discounts on payment services. Bluevine includes free unlimited invoicing, estimates, Tap to Pay, mobile check deposit, and bill pay options spanning same-day ACH, standard ACH, checks, and wires. For business financing, Bluevine provides an embedded Line of Credit up to $250,000, Term Loans up to $500,000 through lending partners, and Small Business Administration (SBA) 7(a) loans up to $350,000 via lenders.

An account maintaining a $50,000 balance on Bluevine Standard yields $650 per year at 1.3% APY when meeting the activity goal, with $0 in monthly maintenance fees. That same balance on Novo yields $1,000 in savings, while Mercury lists its yield option, Treasury, only for balances of $250,000 or more.

Bluevine fits small business owners who want checking balances to earn interest while retaining access to credit lines. Versus Mercury, Bluevine links directly to commercial lending products, but its highest interest rate requires the $95 per month Premier tier, and the base rate depends on meeting a monthly activity goal.

alternatives.heading: Lili Freelance Banking and Embedded Tax Accounting
alternatives.body:
Lili is a financial technology platform offering commercial banking tools. The entry Lili Core plan charges $0 per month and includes a Lili Visa debit card, express ACH, domestic and international wire processing, and up to $3,000,000 in FDIC insurance through sweep program banks. Lili provides variable savings yields of 2.25% APY up to $500,000, rising to 4.00% from $500,000 to $1,000,000 and flexible capital up to $250,000 embedded inside the account.

Lili offers three paid tiers: Lili Pro, Lili Smart, and Lili Premium. The reviewed pages do not publish the monthly fee figures for these paid tiers. Lili reserves debit card cash back exclusively for Pro, Smart, and Premium members. Accounting features, tax preparation software, and invoicing tools are restricted to Smart and Premium subscribers.

Evaluating returns on cash reserves, a business holding $25,000 in savings on Lili at the 2.25% variable APY earns $562.50 per year before accounting for any plan costs. On Mercury, a $25,000 balance does not qualify for Mercury Treasury (which requires $250,000), yielding $0 in interest.

Lili fits businesses that want high savings interest and integrated tax tools. Versus Mercury, Lili restricts tax and invoicing features to paid tiers without publishing monthly prices on its main page, whereas Mercury includes unlimited invoicing on its free plan.

alternatives.heading: Chase Business Complete Banking and Branch Network Access
alternatives.body:
Chase states that more small business owners choose Chase than any other bank. Its entry commercial account, Chase Business Complete Banking, carries a monthly service fee of $15, which can be avoided by meeting published waiver criteria. The account includes up to 20 paper and teller transactions, $5,000 in monthly in-branch cash deposits per statement cycle, and mobile card acceptance.

For higher cash and transaction volumes, Chase provides Performance Business Checking for $40 per month (or $0 if waived), allowing up to 250 account debits, $20,000 in monthly cash deposits, all incoming wires, and the two most expensive outgoing domestic wires per month. Chase Platinum Business Checking costs $95 per month (or $0 if waived), covering 500 account debits, $25,000 in monthly cash deposits, incoming wires, and the four most expensive outgoing wires. Chase waives monthly service fees on business savings accounts when linked to an eligible checking account.

Over 12 statement cycles, Chase Business Complete Banking costs $180 ($15 multiplied by 12) if the fee is not waived. Performance Business Checking costs $480 per year ($40 multiplied by 12), and Platinum Business Checking costs $1,140 per year ($95 multiplied by 12).

Chase fits businesses handling physical cash deposits and requiring local branch support. Versus Mercury, Chase charges monthly fees on standard tiers and limits cash and teller transactions, whereas Mercury provides online accounts with $0 monthly maintenance fees.

alternatives.heading: Wise Business Multi-Currency Accounts and Low-Cost Transfers
alternatives.body:
Wise Business is a cross-border financial platform operated by Wise, which is not an FDIC-insured bank. Wise states that over 900,000 global businesses move $16 billion per month through its service. Registration is free, and the platform has no ongoing subscription plans or monthly maintenance fees. Users see fees upfront and pay only for services utilized.

Wise Business provides local account details in multiple global currencies. Wise Business charges a fixed fee of $6.11 to receive domestic wires in USD. Outgoing wire transfers start as low as $1.13, which Wise compares against typical $25 or higher fees charged by U.S. banks. Wise also provides an opt-in interest feature through a program bank, paying a 3.68% variable APY on USD balances with up to $250,000 in pass-through FDIC coverage.

A company receiving two domestic wires and sending four international wire transfers in a month illustrates the cost structure. At Wise Business, two incoming domestic wires cost $12.22 (two multiplied by $6.11), and four outgoing wires at the $1.13 starting rate cost at least $4.52, totaling at least $16.74. At Mercury, incoming domestic wires and outgoing USD international wires cost $0. If outgoing transfers involve foreign currency conversion, Mercury charges a 1% exchange fee, whereas Wise shows fees upfront.

 Versus Mercury, Wise charges $6.11 to receive domestic wires, while Mercury provides free incoming wires in USD.

alternatives.heading: Brex Corporate Cards and Global Spend Management
alternatives.body:
Brex is a financial technology platform offering business accounts, corporate charge cards, bill pay, and expense management on a single interface. Brex corporate cards are accepted in more than 210 countries and territories. Its Essentials plan costs $0 per user per month, supporting global card acceptance, artificial intelligence (AI) spend rules, up to two legal entities, accounting integrations, local currency wire transfers, free travel booking, real-time reporting, application programming interface (API) access, bill pay, and expense reimbursements.

Brex Premium costs $12 per user per month. It adds multiple customizable expense policies, dynamic review chains, international multi-entity management, enterprise resource planning (ERP) and human resources information system (HRIS) integrations, and live budget tracking. Enterprise and Smart Card plans require custom enterprise pricing and add named account managers and local currency cards across 50 or more countries.

A company with 10 employees using Brex Premium pays $120 per month ($12 multiplied by 10), which totals $1,440 per year. On Brex Essentials, the subscription fee is $0. Mercury's core tier costs $0 with employee spend cards and limits, while Mercury Plus costs $29.90 per month on annual billing ($358.80 per year) and Mercury Pro costs $299 per month ($3,588 per year).

Brex fits organizations that require multi-entity corporate card controls and customizable ERP integrations. Versus Mercury, Brex Premium charges per-seat pricing that scales with team headcount, while Mercury charges flat monthly rates for its Plus and Pro tiers.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
This comparison evaluates published commercial banking fees and software tiers. It is not suitable for several categories of readers:

- Retail consumers seeking personal checking accounts with branch access; these options are evaluated on our [comparison hub](/compare/).
- Businesses with commercial lending needs exceeding $500,000.
- Organizations requiring formal legal or tax counsel regarding corporate entity structure or tax compliance.
- Readers seeking subjective app rankings rather than published fee schedules and account limits.

If you need personal checking tools instead of business accounts, review our dedicated banking guides before comparing commercial accounts.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer
alternatives.body:
The comparison on this page reflects published pricing and account terms as of November 18, 2026. Several operational changes would alter how these providers compare:

- Mercury altering its $0 core plan, changing its $250,000 balance threshold for Mercury Treasury, or adding monthly maintenance fees.
- Chase adjusting its $15 Business Complete Banking fee or changing its waiver requirements.
- Relay updating its 1.19% to 3.21% APY savings tiers, or removing the promotional $90 pricing on Relay Scale.
- Lili publishing standard monthly prices for its Pro, Smart, or Premium tiers, or Bluevine changing its $30 and $95 plan prices.
- Wise Business changing its $6.11 domestic wire receipt charge or its 3.68% variable USD interest rate.
- Novo removing the $50,000 minimum balance requirement to earn 2% APY on Novo Savings.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Mercury Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Mercury remains the closer match for businesses that require fee-free domestic and international wire movement in USD without monthly subscription costs. Mercury's $0 plan includes business checking and savings, up to $5,000,000 in FDIC insurance through sweep networks, free domestic and international USD wires, free check mailing, and real-time payments.

Mercury also integrates corporate credit cards earning 1.5% cash back, custom spend limits, duplicate subscription detection, and free personal banking. For companies holding over $250,000 in cash, Mercury Treasury provides yields up to 4.42% invested in the JPMorgan U.S. Treasury Plus Money Market Fund.

 Compare your expected wire volumes and treasury balances against these parameters before opening an account.

verdict: Mercury provides $0 checking with fee-free USD wires and up to $5M in FDIC insurance, while alternatives offer distinct operational advantages. Relay excels for businesses that separate cash into multiple checking accounts, Chase provides physical branch teller access, Novo reimburses ATM fees with no account minimums, Bluevine pairs checking interest with credit lines, Wise lowers multi-currency transfer costs. Brex delivers advanced corporate card expense policies. Next step: add up your monthly wires, transfers and card spend, then compare the total with each fee row in the table above.

faqs.question: Is Mercury a bank?
faqs.answer: No. Mercury is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services are provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC, with deposit insurance covering bank failure.

faqs.question: Is Mercury free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mercury's core banking plan costs $0 per month with no minimum balances, no overdraft fees, and free domestic and USD international wires. Optional paid tiers include Mercury Plus at $29.90 per month on annual billing ($35 billed monthly) and Mercury Pro at $299 per month.

faqs.question: What are Mercury's fees on international wires?
faqs.answer: Mercury charges $0 for outgoing international wires sent in USD. If you choose optional OUR coding, Mercury charges a flat $15 fee so intermediary charges are covered. International wires sent in foreign currencies incur a 1% currency exchange fee.

faqs.question: Which Mercury alternatives have no monthly fee?
faqs.answer: Relay Starter and Novo both offer $0 monthly fees. Relay Starter includes 20 checking accounts and a 1.19% savings APY, while Novo offers free standard ACH and reimburses ATM fees up to $7 monthly.

faqs.question: Does Mercury pay interest?
faqs.answer: Mercury offers an APY of up to 4.42% through Mercury Treasury for eligible accounts with $250,000 or more in deposits. Funds are invested in the JPMorgan U.S. Treasury Plus Money Market Fund.
