title: Acorns Alternatives 2026: Investing Fees and Plans Compared
h1: Acorns Alternatives 2026: Investing Fees and Plans Compared
metaDescription: Acorns alternatives compared: Stash, Betterment, Wealthfront, Fidelity Go, and Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, with monthly subscriptions and advisory fees.
intro:
Stash, Betterment, Wealthfront, Fidelity Go, and Schwab Intelligent Portfolios are five Acorns alternatives for automated investing. The right choice depends on whether you prefer a flat monthly subscription, an assets under management (AUM) percentage fee, a zero-fee advisory tier, or a dedicated cash allocation.

[Acorns](https://www.acorns.com/) packages its automated micro-investing features into tiered subscriptions: Bronze costs $4 per month, Silver costs $8 per month, and Gold costs $12 per month. Acorns lists no hidden costs or transaction fees, charging just one monthly subscription payment. Acorns Advisers is an investment adviser registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and Acorns Securities provides the brokerage services as a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

Because Acorns uses flat dollar subscriptions rather than a percentage fee, small accounts pay a large share of their balance every year. A person with a $2,000 balance on Acorns Bronze pays $48 per year, which equals an effective annual drag of 2.4%. For a broader survey of robo-investing services, read our [best robo-advisors roundup](/roundup/best-robo-advisors/). If you want a standalone percentage-based fee structure, explore our [Wealthfront alternatives](/alternatives/wealthfront/) guide, browse every comparison in the [comparison hub](/compare/), or see how our [Empower alternatives](/alternatives/empower/) page treats advisory fees.
tableTitle: Acorns Alternatives: Published Fees and Pricing Compared
tableNote: Fees and prices from each provider's own website, checked November 19, 2026.

rows.pricing: Bronze $4 per month, Silver $8 per month, Gold $12 per month. No hidden costs or transaction fees. Investments are not insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and may lose value.
rows.bestFit: Fits investors who want automated spare-change round-ups and a retirement account on the $4 plan, with banking added at $8 and family features at $12

rows.pricing: The Stash Plan costs $12 per month ($108 billed annually). An additional 0.25% annual AUM fee applies to Smart Portfolios of $1,000 or more and Managed Retirement Accounts. 7-day trial.
rows.bestFit: Fits investors who want Stock-Back rewards, DIY stock picks alongside managed portfolios, and a bundled life insurance policy

rows.pricing: Base investing costs $5 per month for balances up to $24,000. Switches to 0.25% annually with $200 monthly deposits or balances of $24,000 or more. Premium tier costs 0.65% annually ($100,000 minimum).
rows.bestFit: Fits investors who want automated portfolios, checking, multiple retirement account types, and recurring deposits that reduce monthly fees

rows.pricing: The Wealthfront Portfolio charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee. Tax-loss harvesting and automatic rebalancing included. Cash account has no fees and a $1 opening minimum.
rows.bestFit: Fits investors seeking a flat 0.25% advisory fee with automated tax-loss harvesting, rebalancing, and a cash account

rows.pricing: $0 annual advisory fee for balances under $25,000. 0.35% annual advisory fee for balances of $25,000 or more. Minimum deposit to begin investing is $10.
rows.bestFit: Fits investors starting with small balances who want zero advisory fees up to $25,000 and access to financial coaching at higher balances

rows.pricing: $0 advisory fee and $0 commissions. Requires a $5,000 minimum deposit to open. A portion of the portfolio is held in cash at Charles Schwab Bank.
rows.bestFit: Fits investors with at least $5,000 who want automated exchange-traded fund (ETF) portfolios with no advisory fee and do not mind holding a cash allocation

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose an Acorns Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting an alternative to Acorns comes down to how your account balance interacts with flat monthly fees versus percentage advisory rates. Acorns charges a flat dollar fee ($4, $8, or $12 per month) regardless of whether your investment balance is $50 or $50,000. On small balances, flat fees create high percentage drag. For example, $4 per month equals $48 per year. On a $500 balance, that $48 fee represents 9.6% of your assets annually. On a $2,000 balance, $48 per year represents 2.4% annually. Conversely, on a $50,000 balance, $48 per year is less than 0.10%.

Percentage-based alternatives charge an annual assets under management (AUM) fee. Wealthfront charges 0.25% per year, meaning an account balance of $2,000 costs $5 per year. Betterment charges $5 per month ($60 per year) on balances under $24,000, but drops to 0.25% per year if you establish recurring deposits of $200 per month or cross the $24,000 mark. At $24,000, Betterment's 0.25% annual fee comes to exactly $60 per year.

Zero-fee alternatives are a third cost model. Fidelity Go charges a $0 advisory fee under $25,000. At $25,000 it charges 0.35% per year. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges no advisory fee or commissions at all. It does require a $5,000 opening deposit, and it keeps part of the portfolio as cash at Charles Schwab Bank, which is insured by the FDIC. Schwab says this cash can pay a lower yield than cash options outside the program.

Four factors drive the comparison:

- Account balance size: Compare the flat monthly fee against an AUM percentage to see which takes fewer dollars out of your portfolio each year.
- Deposit routines: Determine if you plan to deposit spare change through automated round-ups, schedule fixed recurring deposits, or transfer lump sums.
- Account types needed: Check whether you need an individual taxable brokerage account, an individual retirement account (IRA) such as a traditional, Roth, or SEP IRA, or a custodial account for children.
- Cash and banking features: Identify whether you need an integrated checking account with debit card access, fee-free automated teller machines (ATMs), or a separate cash reserve with an annual percentage yield (APY).

alternatives.heading: Stash Subscription Plans and Assets Under Management Fees
alternatives.body:
Stash offers an automated and self-directed investing platform through The Stash Plan, which costs $12 per month, or $108 per year when billed annually (a 25% savings). Stash includes 24/7 financial guidance, a personalized investment plan, Stock-Back rewards worth up to $120 per year, a $10,000 life insurance policy, and a 3% retirement match on contributions worth up to $225 per year. Stash offers a 7-day trial and states no account minimums on its pricing page. It supports taxable brokerage accounts, retirement accounts, and custodial accounts for children. Users can pick individual stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or use managed diversified portfolios.

In addition to the subscription, Stash charges an annual AUM fee of 0.25% on Smart Portfolios with balances of $1,000 or more, as well as on Managed Retirement Accounts. This means a customer using a managed portfolio pays both the subscription and the percentage fee.

Consider an investor with a $5,000 balance in a managed portfolio. On Stash, annual subscription billing costs $108 per year, while the 0.25% AUM fee on $5,000 adds $12.50 per year, bringing the total annual cost to $120.50. On monthly billing ($12 per month), the annual total is $144 plus $12.50, which equals $156.50. On Acorns Bronze, that same $5,000 balance costs $48 per year ($4 per month), while Acorns Gold costs $144 per year ($12 per month) with no additional percentage advisory fee.

Stash falls short of Acorns Bronze on base pricing, since Stash costs $12 per month compared to $4 per month for Acorns Bronze. Stash also adds a 0.25% advisory fee on top of its subscription for managed accounts over $1,000, whereas Acorns includes portfolio management inside its subscription. Stash fits investors who want to combine self-directed stock picks with automated portfolios, use Stock-Back rewards, and access a bundled life insurance policy.

alternatives.heading: Betterment Account Fees and Balance Thresholds
alternatives.body:
Betterment provides automated investing portfolios across individual taxable accounts, traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEP IRAs, Solo 401(k) accounts, and self-directed investing. Its entry pricing lists a base fee of $5 per month for investing balances between $0 and $24,000. That flat fee switches to a 0.25% annual fee if the investor sets up monthly recurring deposits of $200 or more, or when the account balance reaches $24,000. Betterment also offers a Premium tier charging 0.65% annually (composed of a 0.25% Digital base fee plus a 0.40% Premium fee) for accounts with at least $100,000 in eligible household investments, which provides access to an advisor. Betterment Cash Reserve is a high-yield cash account with no fees, no stated balance minimums, and FDIC insurance through program banks. It offers a variable 3.50% APY as of September 21, 2026, alongside a 0.75% APY Boost for new clients who make a qualifying deposit through April 16, 2027.

The cost difference between Acorns and Betterment depends directly on account balance and deposit behavior. On a $2,000 balance with no recurring deposit, Betterment charges $5 per month ($60 per year), which represents a 3.0% annual drag. Acorns Bronze charges $4 per month ($48 per year), representing a 2.4% drag. However, if the investor sets up a $200 monthly deposit, Betterment's fee drops to 0.25% annually. On that $2,000 balance, 0.25% equals $5 per year, saving $43 per year compared to Acorns Bronze.

On larger accounts, Betterment's percentage structure changes the equation. An account with $30,000 pays 0.25% on Betterment, which equals $75 per year. On Acorns Bronze, that same $30,000 account costs $48 per year. On Acorns Silver, it costs $96 per year ($8 per month), and on Acorns Gold, it costs $144 per year ($12 per month).

Betterment falls short of Acorns on micro-investing tooling, as Betterment does not offer spare-change round-ups or partner brand bonus investments. Betterment fits investors who can commit to $200 monthly deposits to unlock a 0.25% fee and manage multiple retirement account types.

alternatives.heading: Wealthfront Flat Percentage Advisory Fee and Cash Account
alternatives.body:
Wealthfront offers automated portfolio management called The Wealthfront Portfolio for an annual advisory fee of 0.25% of assets under management. The fee covers automatic rebalancing and tax-loss harvesting. Wealthfront also offers a self-directed Brokerage Account for individual stocks and ETFs, alongside a Cash account that requires $1 to get started and charges no account fees.

Because Wealthfront charges an advisory percentage rather than a subscription, small accounts pay far less in dollar terms. An investor with an account balance of $2,000 pays 0.25% per year, which totals $5 per year. On Acorns Bronze ($4 per month), the annual fee is $48. Moving to Wealthfront saves that investor $43 per year on portfolio management fees. On an account balance of $10,000, Wealthfront charges $25 per year, while Acorns Bronze still charges $48 per year. The break-even point between Acorns Bronze and Wealthfront arrives at $19,200. At $19,200, a 0.25% annual fee equals exactly $48 per year. Above $19,200, Acorns Bronze charges fewer total dollars per year than Wealthfront.

Against Acorns Gold at $12 per month ($144 per year), the break-even balance on Wealthfront is $57,600 (0.25% of $57,600 equals $144 per year).

Wealthfront falls short of Acorns on checking integrations and micro-saving tools. Wealthfront does not provide spare-change round-ups, nor does it offer bonus investments or tip matching. Wealthfront fits investors who want automated index investing with tax-loss harvesting and no flat monthly fee.

alternatives.heading: Fidelity Go Zero-Fee Tier and Coaching Threshold
alternatives.body:
Fidelity Go provides robo-advisory portfolios with no minimum balance required to open an account. Investing begins once the account balance reaches $10. Fidelity Go charges a $0 annual advisory fee on account balances under $25,000. It publishes no trading fees. Once an account balance reaches $25,000 or more, Fidelity Go charges an annual advisory fee of 0.35% of assets under management. At the $25,000 mark and above, clients also receive unlimited one-on-one financial coaching sessions, along with tax-loss harvesting on taxable accounts holding stock-based Flex Funds.

For balances below $25,000, Fidelity Go costs less than Acorns across all tiers. An investor maintaining a $2,000 balance pays $0 per year on Fidelity Go, compared to $48 per year on Acorns Bronze, $96 per year on Acorns Silver, and $144 per year on Acorns Gold. An investor with a $15,000 balance pays $0 per year on Fidelity Go, saving $48 to $144 every year.

Once the account balance crosses $25,000, Fidelity Go's 0.35% advisory fee takes effect. On a $25,000 balance, 0.35% equals $87.50 per year. On a $40,000 balance, 0.35% equals $140 per year. By comparison, Acorns Bronze remains $48 per year and Acorns Silver remains $96 per year regardless of how large the balance grows.

Fidelity Go falls short of Acorns on lifestyle financial perks. Fidelity Go does not feature round-up deposit triggers, partner brand shopping bonuses, or will preparation services. Fidelity Go fits investors with account balances under $25,000 who want professional automated portfolio management with zero advisory fees.

alternatives.heading: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios Minimum Deposit and Cash Drag
alternatives.body:
Schwab Intelligent Portfolios builds and manages automated portfolios composed of approximately 50 expert-selected ETFs. The service charges a $0 advisory fee and $0 in commissions, though investors pay the underlying ETF operating expenses. It requires a minimum deposit of $5,000 to open an account. Automatic daily monitoring and rebalancing are included, and customer support is available 24/7. Accounts with $50,000 or more can enroll in automated tax-loss harvesting at no additional charge.

A primary feature of Schwab Intelligent Portfolios is that a portion of every portfolio is held in cash deposited at Charles Schwab Bank, a bank insured by the FDIC. Schwab states on its product page that this cash portion can pay a lower yield than cash alternatives outside the program. This lower cash yield functions as cash drag, which offsets the absence of a stated advisory fee.

Comparing expenses to Acorns highlights the starting barrier. Acorns allows investors to open accounts and start investing spare change with no large lump-sum deposit. Schwab requires $5,000 up front. For an investor who deposits $5,000, Schwab charges $0 in annual advisory fees. Acorns Bronze charges $48 per year on that same $5,000, and Acorns Gold charges $144 per year. Over a five-year holding period, avoiding Acorns Bronze's $4 per month fee saves $240 in advisory fees on that $5,000 balance.

Schwab Intelligent Portfolios falls short of Acorns for casual savers who cannot meet the $5,000 opening requirement, and it lacks micro-investing tools like round-up deposits. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios fits investors who have at least $5,000 to invest and want automated ETF rebalancing without ongoing advisory fees.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Automated micro-investing alternatives do not serve every financial requirement:

- Investors who want advisor access at small balances cannot use Betterment Premium, which requires $100,000 in eligible household investments. 

- Investors with under $5,000 who cannot meet opening balance minimums cannot use Schwab Intelligent Portfolios. 
- Investors who do not want a portion of their portfolio held in cash cannot use Schwab Intelligent Portfolios.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Acorns Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Our comparison of Acorns alternatives would shift if providers change their fee schedules, deposit minimums, or account thresholds:

- If Acorns introduces a percentage-based fee tier for small balances instead of its $4, $8, and $12 monthly subscriptions, the fee drag on balances under $2,000 would diminish.
- If Fidelity Go alters its $25,000 free advisory threshold or increases its 0.35% advisory rate, the fee comparison for mid-sized portfolios would change.
- If Betterment removes the $5 monthly flat fee on balances under $24,000 for accounts that lack a $200 recurring monthly deposit, it would become significantly cheaper for small, irregular savers.
- If Schwab Intelligent Portfolios lowers its $5,000 opening minimum or alters how its cash allocation is structured, it would become accessible to entry-level micro-investors.
- If Stash eliminates its $12 monthly base plan in favor of a low flat AUM fee, it would compete more directly with Wealthfront and Betterment.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Acorns Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Acorns remains the better fit for investors who want automated spare-change investing. Acorns provides Round-Ups to save and invest spare change into diversified portfolios. Its Bronze plan ($4 per month) bundles automated investing, Acorns Later retirement accounts, paycheck splitting and educational courses. Acorns lists a 1% match on new individual retirement account (IRA) contributions during the first year under the Silver plan ($8 per month).

For families and broader banking needs, Acorns Gold ($12 per month) bundles features that would otherwise require multiple services. Gold includes checking accounts without overdraft fees, access to 55,000+ fee-free ATMs in the AllPoint network, a 3% IRA match on new contributions during the first year (up to $225 when maxing out the contribution), and investment accounts for children with a 1% match. It also provides the Acorns Early app and debit card for kids, free federal, state, and local tax filing through third-party providers, a $10,000 life insurance policy for eligible customers, and a no-cost Will valued at $299.

Acorns Gold also includes Invest My Tips for workers who receive gratuities. It generates a personalized QR code, invests 100% of each tip received, and adds a 1% match on qualifying tips. For members who qualify for the 3% IRA match ($225 value) and use the third-party tax filing, part of the $144 annual cost of Acorns Gold is returned in benefits. Banking services for Acorns Checking are provided by Lincoln Savings Bank or nbkc bank, members FDIC.

verdict:
Acorns packages micro-investing, retirement accounts, and family banking into monthly subscriptions of $4, $8, and $12. For smaller account balances, percentage-based alternatives like Wealthfront (0.25% AUM) or zero-fee tiers like Fidelity Go ($0 on balances under $25,000) can cost less per year.

The next step for any Acorns alternative is arithmetic: multiply your balance by each percentage fee, set the result beside the $4 to $12 monthly Acorns price, and read the full fee schedule on the provider's site.

faqs.question: How much does Acorns cost per month?
faqs.answer: Acorns offers three subscription plans: Bronze at $4 per month, Silver at $8 per month, and Gold at $12 per month. Acorns lists no hidden transaction fees, charging only the monthly subscription fee.

faqs.question: Is Acorns worth the monthly fee for small balances?
faqs.answer: On small balances, Acorns carries a high percentage cost. A $4 per month fee equals $48 per year, which is a 2.4% annual fee on a $2,000 balance and a 9.6% annual fee on a $500 balance. In contrast, Wealthfront charges 0.25% ($5 per year on $2,000) and Fidelity Go charges $0 on balances under $25,000.

faqs.question: Which Acorns alternative has no monthly advisory fee?
faqs.answer: Fidelity Go charges a $0 annual advisory fee on account balances under $25,000. Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges a $0 advisory fee and $0 commissions, but requires a $5,000 minimum deposit and allocates a portion of assets to Charles Schwab Bank cash.

faqs.question: Does Acorns charge an assets under management percentage fee?
faqs.answer: No. Acorns charges flat subscription fees of $4, $8, or $12 per month rather than a percentage of assets under management. However, Stash charges both a $12 monthly subscription and an annual 0.25% AUM fee on managed portfolios of $1,000 or more.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest robo-advisor for balances under $25,000?
faqs.answer: Fidelity Go charges a $0 advisory fee on balances under $25,000, while Schwab Intelligent Portfolios also charges a $0 advisory fee but requires $5,000 to open. Wealthfront charges 0.25% annually ($2.50 per year per $1,000 invested), while Betterment charges 0.25% if you deposit at least $200 per month.

title: Wave Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Features Compared
h1: Wave Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Features Compared
metaDescription: Wave alternatives compared: QuickBooks Online, FreshBooks, Xero, Zoho Books and Bonsai, with published plan prices, user limits and processing fees.
intro:
QuickBooks Online, FreshBooks, Xero, Zoho Books and Bonsai are five Wave alternatives. Zoho Books has a free plan, and the paid entry plans start at $15 to $38 per month. The right choice depends on whether you need a free tier, plans priced by client or invoice count, multi-user accounting, project and inventory tracking, or time tracking with proposals and contracts. The table lists each plan's published price, and the sections below add up user fees, add-ons and payment rates over a full year.

[Wave](https://www.waveapps.com/) lists a Starter plan at $0 with unlimited invoices, estimates, bills and bookkeeping records, while charging 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0.60 per American Express (Amex) transaction. Wave Pro lists at $19 United States Dollars (USD) per month billed monthly or $190 USD per year, which is also listed at $25 Canadian Dollars (CAD) per month or $250 CAD per year. Wave Pro adds automatic bank transaction imports through Plaid, automated categorization, receipt capture and a 2.9% + $0 transaction fee on the first 10 credit card payments each month.

For other accounting and billing shortlists, see the [QuickBooks alternatives](/alternatives/quickbooks/) guide, the [FreshBooks alternatives](/alternatives/freshbooks/) comparison, and the [best accounting software for freelancers roundup](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/). Readers can also browse the [comparison hub](/compare/) for wider software breakdowns.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Wave Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with user seats. Wave Starter adds no extra user roles. Wave Pro lets owners invite contributors as admin, editor or viewer for $19 per month. QuickBooks Online prices access by tier, from 1 user on Simple Start to 25 on Advanced. Zoho Books gives 3 users on Standard for $20 per month. FreshBooks adds $11 per month for each extra team member.

Next, look at card fees. Wave charges 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction on Starter. On a $1,000 customer invoice, that transaction fee equals $29.60. On Wave Pro, the fixed $0.60 fee is removed for the first 10 card transactions each month, which reduces the fee to $29.00 per $1,000 transaction. 

Last, ask whether the main job is full accounting records or plain client invoicing. Wave provides estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records. Xero provides bank reconciliation, while Zoho Books includes bank feeds. Bonsai provides customer relationship management (CRM), contracts, scheduling, proposals and invoicing.

alternatives.heading: QuickBooks Online Plans and Multi-User Accounting
alternatives.body:
QuickBooks Online is an accounting application with tiered plans. Simple Start lists at $38 per month for 1 user and 2 accountant seats, covering income and expense tracking, basic reports, one connected bank and two invoices per month in the plan description. Essentials lists at $85 per month for 3 users, adding bulk invoice creation in beta, enhanced reporting and quarterly tax payment estimates. Plus lists at $140 per month for 5 users, introducing inventory tracking, project profitability and automatic bank reconciliation. Advanced costs $340 per month for up to 25 users, adding custom key performance indicators (KPIs), automated workflows and granular user permissions.

QuickBooks Online fits businesses that need inventory tracking and multi-user access controls.

 Wave Pro billed monthly costs $19 per month, which equals $228 per year. QuickBooks Online Simple Start costs $38 per month, totaling $456 per year. QuickBooks Online Plus costs $140 per month, which totals $1,680 per year. Selecting QuickBooks Online Plus instead of Wave Pro represents an annual subscription difference of $1,452.

 Wave provides unlimited invoicing and bookkeeping for $0 on its Starter plan, whereas QuickBooks Online requires an ongoing monthly fee of at least $38 following its 3-month introductory discount.

alternatives.heading: FreshBooks Client Limits and Invoicing Tools
alternatives.body:
FreshBooks is an invoicing and client billing application with tiered client limits. Lite lists at $23 per month and allows billing up to 5 active clients, along with expense tracking, estimates and tax-time reporting. Plus lists at $43 per month for up to 50 clients, adding client retainers, proposals, receipt scanning and accountant access. Premium lists at $70 per month and supports unlimited billable clients, customized email templates and project profitability tracking. FreshBooks also offers a custom-priced Select tier.

FreshBooks fits businesses that require integrated client proposals and client retainers. FreshBooks adds client retainers, proposals and project profitability tracking.

Evaluating the costs based on client count reveals clear differences. Wave allows unlimited billable clients on both its $0 Starter plan and its $19 monthly Pro plan. A business billing 25 clients lands on FreshBooks Plus at $43 per month, which totals $516 per year. If that business adds 2 team members at $11 per user per month, the FreshBooks subscription rises to $65 per month, or $780 per year. Wave Pro for that same team lists at $19 per month on Pro with no per-user price on its pricing page, which is $552 less per year than $780.

 A company invoicing 60 clients on FreshBooks must choose the $70 per month Premium tier ($840 annually), whereas Wave supports unlimited clients on its $0 Starter plan.

alternatives.heading: Xero Features and Invoice Caps
alternatives.body:
Xero is an accounting platform supporting bank reconciliation, bill tracking and reporting. In the United States, Early lists at $27 per month and allows quotes and 20 invoices per month and 5 bills, while providing bank reconciliation, 30-day cash flow forecasting and online invoice payment options. Growing lists at $59 per month, removing those caps, and adding automated bill entry, and a 60-day cash flow forecast. Established lists at $97 per month, adding multi-currency transactions, project time and cost tracking, employee expense claims and a 180-day cash flow forecast.

Xero fits businesses that need bank reconciliation and cash flow forecasting. Wave charges $19 per month on Pro to access user permissions and bank transaction categorization.

The arithmetic shifts based on monthly transaction volume. A business sending 30 invoices per month exceeds the Early plan cap of 20 invoices and must subscribe to Xero Growing at $59 per month, which totals $708 per year. Wave Pro costs $190 per year when billed annually, creating an annual savings of $518 compared to Xero Growing. On regular monthly billing, Xero Early costs $27 x 12 = $324 per year, whereas Wave Starter costs $0.

Xero falls short of Wave on entry-level billing allowances. Wave Starter permits unlimited invoices for $0, while Xero Early restricts users to 20 invoices per month at $27 per month.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Books Free Plan and Scaled Tiers
alternatives.body:
Zoho Books is a cloud accounting software suite with multiple operational tiers. Its Free plan costs $0 per month for 1 user and 1 accountant, limited to revenue under $50K per financial year and 1,000 invoices and 1,000 expenses per year. It supports invoices, quotes, expense logging, receipt auto-scans, mileage tracking and online payments. Standard lists at $20 per month ($15 per month billed annually) for 3 users, adding bank feeds, progress invoicing, 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC e-filing and application programming interface (API) access. Professional costs $50 per month ($40 billed annually) for 5 users, introducing purchase orders, multi-currency accounting, timesheet billing, project profitability and inventory tracking.

Zoho Books fits businesses that require inventory tracking, progress invoicing and 1099 filing. 

Comparing the annual costs demonstrates the value of Zoho Books for multi-user setups. A three-person company on Zoho Books Standard billed annually pays $15 x 12 = $180 per year. Wave Pro billed annually costs $190 per year. On monthly billing, Zoho Books Standard is $20 per month ($240 per year) compared to $19 per month ($228 per year) for Wave Pro. For 5 users needing inventory tools, Zoho Books Professional billed annually costs $40 x 12 = $480 per year.

alternatives.heading: Bonsai Per-User Pricing for Contracts and Billing
alternatives.body:
Bonsai is a business management and invoicing platform with per-user pricing. Bonsai charges on a per-user, per-month schedule. On monthly billing, Basic costs $15, Essentials costs $25, Premium costs $39 and Elite costs $59 per user. On annual billing, the rates drop to $9, $19, $29 and $49 per user per month. Basic covers time tracking, task management, client management (CRM), unlimited projects and unlimited clients. Invoicing, online payments, contracts, proposals, scheduling, client portals and expense tracking begin at the Essentials tier.

Bonsai fits businesses that require contracts, proposals, scheduling and invoicing in one subscription. 

Examining multi-user agency pricing highlights the difference in billing structures. A two-person team using Bonsai Essentials on monthly billing pays 2 x $25 = $50 per month, totaling $600 per year. On annual billing, the same two users pay 2 x $19 = $38 per month, or $456 per year. Wave Pro costs $19 per month ($228 per year) or $190 billed annually, with no per-user price listed on its pricing page. Choosing Wave Pro over Bonsai Essentials saves that two-person team $266 per year on annual billing.

 Bonsai includes income and expense tracking starting on Essentials, while Wave includes bookkeeping records on its Starter plan.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Wave and its alternatives leave some businesses out.

- Wave fits poorly for businesses that need inventory tracking or granular multi-user permissions. Wave's pricing page lists neither on Starter.
- QuickBooks Online fits poorly for solo owners who only invoice, since the lowest plan is $38 per month.
- FreshBooks fits poorly for businesses with more than 50 clients, because only Premium at $70 per month covers unlimited billable clients.
- Zoho Books Free fits poorly for businesses with revenue of $50K or more per financial year.
- Bonsai fits poorly for larger teams, because every plan is priced per user per month.
- Wave Advisors is a separate bookkeeping service starting at $149 per month. It is not part of the $0 Starter plan.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Wave Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Several pricing moves or functional updates could alter the comparative value of these platforms:

- Wave modifying its $0 Starter plan by placing caps on invoice volume, active clients or bookkeeping records.
- Wave expanding the discounted 2.9% + $0 credit card rate on Wave Pro beyond the current cap of 10 transactions per month.
- QuickBooks Online altering the monthly list prices for Simple Start ($38), Essentials ($85) or Plus ($140).
- Xero removing or adjusting the 20-invoice and 5-bill monthly limit on its $27 Early plan.
- Zoho Books changing the user allowances on its Standard ($20 per month for 3 users) or Professional ($50 per month for 5 users) tiers.
- Bonsai adjusting its per-user pricing model.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Wave Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Wave fits businesses that want bookkeeping records and unlimited invoicing without a monthly subscription fee. Wave Starter delivers unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records for $0. 

For businesses wanting automated bank feeds, Wave Pro at $19 per month billed monthly or $190 per year billed annually costs less than QuickBooks Online Simple Start at $38 per month or Xero Early at $27 per month. Wave Pro also includes unlimited receipt scanning using optical character recognition (OCR), auto-categorization of transactions and automated late payment reminders sent at 3, 7 and 14 days past the invoice due date.

Wave also integrates optional services when needed. Owners can add Wave Advisors bookkeeping starting at $149 per month for monthly financial statements, payroll starting from $25 or $40 per month, and live chat or email support operating Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 4:45 PM Eastern.

verdict:
Wave Starter delivers $0 invoicing and bookkeeping records, while Wave Pro provides automated bank feeds and receipt capture for $19 per month. QuickBooks Online fits businesses that need inventory management and granular user roles. Xero fits businesses that want cash flow forecasting and bank reconciliation. Zoho Books fits those that want project profitability and inventory tracking, and Bonsai fits those that bundle proposals, contracts and scheduling with billing.

For a Wave alternative, the concrete next step is to count your user seats and monthly client invoices, then read the matching plan row in the table above.

faqs.question: Is Wave really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wave Starter costs $0 per month and includes unlimited invoices, estimates, bills and bookkeeping records. Wave charges optional fees for payment processing, optional receipt scanning, payroll and live support.

faqs.question: How does Wave make money?
faqs.answer: Wave generates revenue through transaction processing fees on credit card and American Express payments, monthly subscriptions for Wave Pro ($19 USD per month), receipt capture add-ons, payroll processing and Wave Advisors bookkeeping services.

faqs.question: What does Wave Pro cost?
faqs.answer: Wave Pro costs $19 USD per month when billed monthly or $190 USD per year when billed annually. In Canada, it lists at $25 CAD per month or $250 CAD per year. It adds automated bank transaction imports, receipt capture, automated late payment reminders and discounted payment processing.

faqs.question: Does Wave charge for credit card payments?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wave Starter charges 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0.60 per American Express transaction. Wave Pro discounts credit card processing to 2.9% + $0 for the first 10 transactions each month.

faqs.question: Which Wave alternative has the most users included?
faqs.answer: User allowances vary: QuickBooks Online Advanced includes up to 25 users, Zoho Books Ultimate includes 15 users, and Bonsai charges per user. In contrast, QuickBooks Online limits Simple Start to 1 user and Essentials to 3 users, Zoho Books Standard covers 3 users, and Bonsai charges per user.

From $25,000, unlimited 1-on-1 coaching calls and tax-loss harvesting on taxable accounts in Flex Funds holding stocks. IRA, health savings account (HSA) or taxable account.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Stash Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the balance you plan to hold, because flat fees and percentage fees cost different amounts at different balances. Stash, Acorns, Robinhood Gold and Betterment's base price charge a flat monthly amount. Wealthfront, Fidelity Go from $25,000 and Betterment after qualifying deposits charge a percentage of assets.

Stash combines both models. On a $10,000 Smart Portfolio, Stash costs $108 plus 0.25% of $10,000 ($25), or $133 a year on annual billing. On monthly billing, the same account costs $144 plus $25, or $169 a year.

That combination sets two break-even points. Wealthfront charges the same 0.25% rate, so a Stash Smart Portfolio of $1,000 or more costs $108 more per year than Wealthfront at the same balance on annual billing. Fidelity Go charges 0.35% from $25,000, which is 0.10% more than Stash's rate, and 0.10% of $108,000 is $108, so Fidelity Go costs less than a Stash Smart Portfolio below $108,000 and more above it.

Next, price the extras. Stash, Acorns Gold and Robinhood Gold each list a 3% retirement or IRA match capped at $225. Acorns limits its Gold match to new contributions in the first year, and Robinhood requires one year on Gold and five years of IRA assets for the full match.

Cash yield is a separate line in the comparison. Robinhood Gold lists 3.6% APY on eligible brokerage cash, Acorns Emergency Savings lists 3.59%, Betterment Cash Reserve lists 3.50% and the M1 High-Yield Cash Account lists 3.35%. Acorns and Betterment describe their rates as variable, and the Stash pricing page lists no cash APY.

Last, match the account type. Stash offers personal brokerage, retirement, custodial accounts for kids and Smart Portfolios. M1 adds joint, trust, Traditional IRA, Roth IRA and Simplified Employee Pension (SEP) IRA accounts, while Fidelity Go covers IRA, HSA and taxable accounts.

alternatives.heading: Stash vs Acorns Pricing by Tier
alternatives.body:
Acorns sells three monthly tiers: Bronze at $4, Silver at $8 and Gold at $12. Every tier includes an investment account with an expert-built diversified portfolio, Round-Ups, the Acorns Later retirement account, Earn bonus investments and Learn courses. Acorns Checking lists no overdraft fees and 55,000+ fee-free automated teller machines (ATMs).

Silver adds a 1% IRA match on new contributions in the first year. Gold raises that match to 3%, up to $225 on a maxed annual contribution according to Acorns. Gold also adds Early Invest for kids, Custom Portfolios of individual stocks and ETFs, a $10,000 life insurance policy for eligible customers and a no-cost Will valued at $299.

Acorns Gold fits people who want Stash-style perks plus Round-Ups, checking, tax filing through third-party providers, and allowance and chore tools. As an illustration on list prices, Acorns Gold costs $12 x 12 = $144 per year, the same as Stash on monthly billing. Stash billed annually costs $108, which is $36 less than Acorns Gold.

Acorns Bronze costs $4 x 12 = $48 per year, which is $60 less than Stash on annual billing. Bronze carries no IRA match, because the match starts at Silver. Acorns Silver costs $8 x 12 = $96 per year for a 1% first-year match.

Acorns falls short of Stash on billing options and match timing. Acorns lists only monthly tier prices, while Stash offers the $108 annual price. Acorns lists its Gold match on new contributions in the first year, while Stash describes its 3% match as worth up to $225 per year.

alternatives.heading: Betterment Base Price and Percentage Fee
alternatives.body:
Betterment charges a base price of $5 per month on investing accounts, which is $5 x 12 = $60 per year. The fee switches to 0.25% a year once recurring deposits total $200 or more per month or balances reach $24,000 or more across Betterment investing accounts. Betterment has no minimum balance, and fund expenses are charged in addition to Betterment's fees.

Betterment Premium costs 0.65% a year, requires $100,000 in eligible investments and adds access to advisors. Balances over $1 million get lower rates: 0.15% for $1 million to $2 million and 0.10% above $2 million. Cash Reserve lists a 3.50% variable APY as of 9/21/2026, plus an added 0.75% on balances up to $1 million for new clients with a qualifying deposit.

Betterment Checking lists no overdraft fees and reimburses ATM fees. Cash Reserve lists no fees.

Betterment fits people who want a percentage fee with no separate subscription once deposits qualify. As an illustration, a $10,000 balance with $200 in monthly deposits costs 0.25% of $10,000, or $25 a year, before fund expenses. The same balance in a Stash Smart Portfolio costs $133 a year on annual billing, a gap of $108.

Betterment falls short of Stash on bundled perks. Betterment's pricing lists no retirement match, life insurance policy or stock rewards, while The Stash Plan includes all three. At $100,000, Betterment Premium costs 0.65% of $100,000, or $650 a year, against $108 plus $250, or $358, for a Stash Smart Portfolio on annual billing.

alternatives.heading: Wealthfront Advisory Fee and Fee-Free Brokerage
alternatives.body:
Wealthfront charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee on the Wealthfront Portfolio, with no monthly subscription. Wealthfront describes tax-loss harvesting as covering that fee for many Classic portfolio clients. The Wealthfront Brokerage Account lists no fees and $1 to get started, for buying ETFs and stocks without advisory or management fees.

Wealthfront fits people who want a managed portfolio priced only as a percentage, or a fee-free account for buying ETFs and stocks. As an illustration, a $10,000 Wealthfront Portfolio costs 0.25% of $10,000, or $25 a year. A $10,000 Stash Smart Portfolio costs $133 a year on annual billing, so Wealthfront costs $108 less at that balance.

At $50,000, the Wealthfront Portfolio fee is 0.25% of $50,000, or $125 a year. A $50,000 Stash Smart Portfolio costs $108 plus $125, or $233 a year on annual billing. The $108 gap stays the same at every balance, because both charge 0.25%.

Wealthfront falls short of Stash on extras bundled into the price. Wealthfront's pricing lists a Cash Account that earns an APY, but no retirement match, life insurance policy or stock rewards. The [Wealthfront alternatives](/alternatives/wealthfront/) comparison covers providers priced against Wealthfront.

alternatives.heading: Robinhood Gold Price and IRA Match
alternatives.body:
Robinhood Gold costs $5 per month, which is $5 x 12 = $60 per year, and the first 30 days are free. Gold pays 3.6% APY on eligible brokerage cash with no cap and no minimum. Gold also adds a 3% match on IRA contributions, up to $225 based on the 2026 maximum.

The full Robinhood match requires one year on Gold and five years of assets in the IRA. Gold also allows deposits up to 3x portfolio value and offers Robinhood Strategies managed portfolios with no management fees above $100,000 for Gold members. Futures cost $0.50 per contract, index options cost $0.35 per contract and instant withdrawal costs a 1.5% fee.

Robinhood Gold fits people who want an IRA match the same size as Stash's at a lower subscription price. On published prices, Gold costs $60 a year against $108 for Stash billed annually, a $48 gap, or $84 less than Stash billed monthly. As an illustration, $5,000 of eligible brokerage cash at 3.6% APY would earn $180 over a year if the rate held.

Robinhood falls short of Stash on life insurance and stock rewards. The Stash Plan includes a $10,000 life insurance policy and Stock-Back rewards worth up to $120 per year, and Robinhood Gold lists neither. Stash describes itself as built for long-term investing and says it is not built for day trading.

Instant withdrawal adds a cost Stash does not list: a $1,000 instant withdrawal at 1.5% costs $15. The [Robinhood Gold breakdown](/guides/is-robinhood-gold-worth-it/) and the [Robinhood alternatives](/alternatives/robinhood/) guide cover Gold in more depth.

alternatives.heading: M1 Platform Fee and Account Types
alternatives.body:
M1 charges no commission, trading or management fees on self-directed brokerage accounts. M1 adds a $3 monthly platform fee, which M1 waives for clients with more than $10,000 at M1. Other fees may apply, including regulatory, account closure and American depositary receipt fees.

M1 Advisor is a free advisory service for M1 clients. The M1 High-Yield Cash Account lists 3.35% APY on uninvested cash. Margin is available on accounts with at least $2,000 in eligible securities.

M1 account types include individual, joint, custodial, Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, SEP IRA and trust accounts. Stash lists personal brokerage, retirement, custodial and Smart Portfolio accounts. M1 fits people who need a joint, trust or SEP IRA account alongside self-directed investing.

As an illustration, an $8,000 M1 account pays $3 x 12 = $36 a year. An $8,000 Stash Smart Portfolio costs $108 plus 0.25% of $8,000 ($20), or $128, on annual billing. At $15,000, M1 waives its platform fee, while the Stash Smart Portfolio costs $108 plus $37.50, or $145.50.

M1 falls short of Stash on perks. The Stash Plan includes a 3% retirement match, a $10,000 life insurance policy and Stock-Back rewards. M1's pricing lists none of those three.

alternatives.heading: Fidelity Go Fee Threshold at $25,000
alternatives.body:
Fidelity Go charges no advisory fee on balances under $25,000 and 0.35% a year at $25,000 and above. Fidelity Go has no minimum to open, and investing starts at $10, since the balance must be at least $10 to invest. Accounts can be an IRA, an HSA or a taxable account, invested in a mix of mutual funds.

From $25,000, Fidelity Go adds unlimited 1-on-1 financial coaching calls. Tax-loss harvesting also starts at $25,000, on taxable accounts in Flex Funds holding stocks.

Fidelity Go fits people with balances under $25,000 who want a managed account with no advisory fee. As an illustration, a $20,000 Fidelity Go account pays $0 in advisory fees, while a $20,000 Stash Smart Portfolio costs $108 plus $50, or $158, on annual billing. At $30,000, Fidelity Go costs 0.35% of $30,000, or $105, against $108 plus $75, or $183, at Stash.

Fidelity Go falls short of Stash at large balances and on perks. Above $108,000, the 0.35% rate costs more than a Stash Smart Portfolio's $108 plus 0.25% on annual billing. At $120,000, for example, Fidelity Go costs $420 a year and the Stash Smart Portfolio costs $108 plus $300, or $408.

Fidelity Go lists no retirement match, life insurance policy or stock rewards. The Stash Plan includes all three for $108 a year on annual billing.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Each option on this list leaves some buyers out, and each has a listed alternative.

- Stash fits poorly for day traders, because Stash says it is built for long-term investing. Robinhood Gold lists futures and index options pricing instead.
- Stash fits poorly for large Smart Portfolio balances when the perks go unused. At $50,000, Stash costs $233 a year on annual billing against $125 at Wealthfront's 0.25% fee.
- Acorns Bronze fits poorly for people who want an IRA match, since the match starts at Silver. Acorns Silver lists a 1% first-year match and Gold lists 3%.
- Betterment Premium fits poorly for accounts under $100,000, the listed minimum. Betterment's standard investing accounts carry no minimum balance.
- Robinhood Gold fits poorly for people who may cancel Gold within a year or move IRA assets within five years, because the full match requires both. Stash describes its 3% match as worth up to $225 per year with no listed holding period.
- Fidelity Go fits poorly for people who want coaching calls on balances under $25,000, because coaching starts at $25,000. Stash includes money coaching from a registered investment advisor.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Stash Alternatives
alternatives.body:
These published price or feature moves would change the comparisons above:

- Stash changing The Stash Plan from $12 per month or $108 per year.
- Stash removing or changing the 0.25% advisory fee on Smart Portfolios of $1,000 or more.
- Acorns extending its Gold 3% IRA match beyond new contributions in the first year.
- Betterment changing the $200 monthly deposit or $24,000 balance thresholds that switch its $5 fee to 0.25%.
- Robinhood changing the $5 Gold price or the one-year and five-year conditions on its 3% IRA match.
- M1 moving its platform fee waiver from more than $10,000.
- Fidelity Go moving its $25,000 threshold or its 0.35% rate, which would move the $108,000 break-even against Stash.
- Any change to the cash rates at Acorns, Betterment, Robinhood or M1.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Stash Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Stash fits people who want guidance, a retirement match, life insurance and stock rewards under one flat subscription. The Stash Plan costs $108 billed annually and includes a 3% retirement match worth up to $225 per year and Stock-Back rewards worth up to $120 per year. Those two listed maximums add up to $345, against the $108 annual price.

The plan also includes 24/7 financial guidance, a personalized investment plan, a $10,000 life insurance policy, budgeting tools and direct deposit up to 2 days early. Expert money coaching comes from a registered investment advisor, and Stash is registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as an investment advisor. Banking runs through Stride Bank N.A., a member of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC).

Stash lists fractional shares from $5 or less across thousands of stocks and ETFs, plus custodial accounts for kids. Stash says it has over 1 million investors, offers a 7-day trial and allows cancellation any time. Stash also lists no banking overdraft charges and no add-on transaction fees.

verdict:
Stash costs $108 a year on annual billing plus 0.25% on Smart Portfolios of $1,000 or more, and its perks list up to $345 a year in combined match and Stock-Back value. 

For Stash alternatives, the concrete next step is to write down the balance you plan to invest and your monthly deposit, then read the matching row in the table above.

faqs.question: How much does Stash cost per month?
faqs.answer: The Stash Plan costs $12 per month, or $108 billed annually, which Stash lists as a 25% saving. Billed monthly, the plan costs $12 x 12 = $144 per year. Stash also charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee on Smart Portfolios with balances of $1,000 or more and on Managed Retirement Accounts.

faqs.question: Is Stash worth it compared with a percentage-fee robo-advisor?
faqs.answer: On fees alone, Wealthfront and Fidelity Go cost less than a Stash Smart Portfolio at $10,000. At $10,000, a Stash Smart Portfolio costs $133 a year on annual billing, against $25 at Wealthfront's 0.25% fee and $0 at Fidelity Go under $25,000. Stash lists a retirement match worth up to $225 per year and Stock-Back rewards worth up to $120 per year, which add up to $345 in listed maximum value against the $108 annual fee.

faqs.question: Does Stash charge an advisory fee on top of the subscription?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stash charges a 0.25% annual AUM advisory fee on Smart Portfolios with balances of $1,000 or more and on Managed Retirement Accounts, in addition to the $12 monthly or $108 annual plan price. On a $10,000 Smart Portfolio, that advisory fee is $25 a year.

faqs.question: Which Stash alternatives have no monthly subscription?
faqs.answer: Wealthfront and Fidelity Go charge a percentage of assets instead of a monthly subscription. Wealthfront charges 0.25% a year on the Wealthfront Portfolio, and Fidelity Go charges $0 under $25,000 and 0.35% from $25,000. Betterment switches from $5 per month to 0.25% with $200 or more in monthly recurring deposits or $24,000 or more in balances, and M1 waives its $3 monthly platform fee above $10,000.

faqs.question: Can I cancel Stash at any time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stash says The Stash Plan can be cancelled any time. Stash also offers a 7-day trial.

title: Betterment Alternatives Compared by Fees and Minimums
h1: Betterment Alternatives Compared by Fees and Minimums
metaDescription: Betterment alternatives compared: Wealthfront, Schwab, Vanguard, Fidelity Go, Acorns, Ally and M1 by advisory fee, account minimum and bundled accounts.
intro:
Wealthfront, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, Vanguard Digital Advisor, Fidelity Go, Acorns, Ally Invest Robo Portfolios and M1 are seven Betterment alternatives for automated investing. They differ on advisory fee (0.25% a year at Wealthfront, no advisory fee at Schwab, no fee under $25,000 at Fidelity Go), on account minimum ($5,000 at Schwab, $100 at Vanguard and Ally, $10 at Fidelity Go) and on what comes bundled, such as checking, cash accounts or spare-change investing. We read each provider's own pricing page on November 20, 2026 and worked out the yearly cost at the balances where the fee rules change.

[Betterment](https://www.betterment.com/pricing) charges $5 per month for automated investing on balances from $0 to $24,000, with no minimum balance. The fee moves to 0.25% a year once recurring deposits total $200 or more a month, or once Betterment investing balances reach $24,000. Exchange-traded fund (ETF) costs inside each portfolio are charged on top of that fee and set by each fund.

Betterment Premium charges 0.65% a year on the first $1 million, requires a $100,000 household minimum and adds access to an advisor. Betterment also offers checking, individual retirement accounts (IRAs), self-directed trading with no commissions and a Cash Reserve account at a variable 3.50% annual percentage yield (APY) as of September 21, 2026. Cash Reserve carries Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) insurance through Program Banks, while Betterment's investments are not FDIC insured and may lose value.

For wider shortlists, see the [best robo-advisors roundup](/roundup/best-robo-advisors/), the [Wealthfront alternatives](/alternatives/wealthfront/) and [Acorns alternatives](/alternatives/acorns/) pages, and the [best high-yield savings accounts roundup](/roundup/best-high-yield-savings-accounts/) for cash-only options. The [comparison hub](/compare/) collects more side-by-side money comparisons.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Betterment Alternative
chooseSection.body:
A Betterment alternative is easiest to compare on two numbers: the invested balance and the monthly deposit. Betterment's fee depends on both, so one $10,000 account can cost $60 a year or $25 a year.

At $10,000 with no recurring deposits, Betterment charges $5 a month, which is $60 a year. With recurring deposits of $200 or more a month, the same $10,000 moves to 0.25%, which is $25 a year. At $24,000 both rules land on $60, because 0.25% of $24,000 is $60.

Next, work out the yearly advisory or subscription cost at your own balance. At $30,000, the published fees come to these amounts:

- Betterment Digital: 0.25%, or $75 a year.
- Wealthfront: 0.25%, or $75 a year.
- Schwab Intelligent Portfolios: $0 advisory fee.
- Vanguard Digital Advisor: about $45 to $48 a year on Vanguard's all-index approximation.
- Fidelity Go: 0.35%, or $105 a year.
- Acorns: $48, $96 or $144 a year for Bronze, Silver or Gold.
- Ally Invest Robo Portfolios: $0 on the cash-enhanced version, or 0.30%, which is $90 a year.
- M1: $0, because the $3 monthly platform fee is waived above $10,000.

Fund expense ratios are charged on top of every figure in that list and are set by each fund. Betterment says its portfolio ETFs carry embedded fund fees and that it receives no part of them.

Last, compare what comes bundled. Betterment and Acorns both offer checking, and Betterment, M1 and Acorns each publish an APY on a cash, savings or checking product. Acorns adds Round-Ups on every plan and IRA matches on its Silver and Gold plans.

If you already use Betterment, moving each investing account to another company costs a flat $75 per account. Withdrawals to a linked checking account carry no fee.

alternatives.heading: Betterment vs Wealthfront on Advisory Fees
alternatives.body:
Wealthfront charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee for The Wealthfront Portfolio, the same percentage Betterment charges once an account qualifies for its 0.25% rate. Wealthfront's own example shows a $15,000 balance at $3.18 per month. On $30,000, 0.25% comes to $75 a year at either company.

The two fee schedules differ below $24,000. Wealthfront's published fee for The Wealthfront Portfolio is the 0.25% rate, which on $10,000 comes to $25 a year. Betterment charges $60 a year on that $10,000 unless recurring deposits reach $200 a month.

Wealthfront lists automatic trades, expert-built portfolios, fully customizable allocations with hundreds of funds, Tax-Loss Harvesting and automatic rebalancing. Its app tracks net worth and links outside accounts. The separate Brokerage Account charges no advisory or management fees on stocks and ETFs and takes $1 to start.

Wealthfront also offers a Cash Account, though Wealthfront's pricing page states no Cash Account APY. Wealthfront fits investors who want to customize allocations from hundreds of funds at a flat 0.25%. More options built around Wealthfront sit on the [Wealthfront alternatives](/alternatives/wealthfront/) page.

alternatives.heading: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios with No Advisory Fee
alternatives.body:
Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges no advisory fee and no commissions, and it takes $5,000 to open. Investors pay the operating expenses of the ETFs in the portfolio, including Schwab ETFs. Schwab says it earns revenue from sources other than an advisory fee.

Part of each portfolio is held as an FDIC-insured deposit at Charles Schwab Bank. The size of that cash allocation is based on the investor's risk profile. Schwab says some cash alternatives outside the program pay a higher yield.

On $30,000, Betterment at 0.25% charges $75 a year and Schwab charges $0 in advisory fees. Tax-loss harvesting is available on taxable portfolios of $50,000 or more at no extra fee, with enrollment required. Schwab lists 24/7 live support from U.S.-based service professionals.

Schwab Intelligent Portfolios fits investors with at least $5,000 who want no advisory fee. Below $5,000, Fidelity Go starts investing at $10 and Vanguard Digital Advisor enrolls at $100.

alternatives.heading: Vanguard Digital Advisor Fees per $10,000
alternatives.body:
Vanguard Digital Advisor charges $0 advisory fees for the first 90 days and requires $100 in assets to enroll. Investment costs still apply during those 90 days. Vanguard approximates the yearly cost of an all-index portfolio at about $15 to $16 per $10,000.

On $30,000, that approximation works out to about $45 to $48 a year, against $75 at Betterment's 0.25% rate. An option with active funds, which may include 3 exclusive Advice Select funds, carries a higher advisory fee of no more than $20 per $10,000 a year. On $30,000, that cap equals $60 a year.

Vanguard lists a personalized risk assessment and planning for multiple goals, such as retirement, a house or education. Its tools include a goal optimizer, a debt payoff calculator and a rainy day emergency fund tool. Vanguard also lists tax-loss harvesting and an option to keep certain holdings at enrollment.

Vanguard Digital Advisor fits investors who want goal-based planning tools with a $100 start.

alternatives.heading: Fidelity Go Fees Above and Below $25,000
alternatives.body:
Fidelity Go has no minimum to open an account and starts investing once the balance reaches $10. It charges $0 in advisory fees under $25,000 and 0.35% a year at $25,000 and above. Fidelity Go lists no trading, transaction or rebalancing fees.

Below $25,000, Fidelity Go charges less in advisory fees than Betterment's $5 monthly charge, which is $60 a year. Above $25,000 the order flips: 0.35% of $40,000 is $140 a year, against $100 at Betterment's 0.25% rate. At $100,000, Fidelity Go comes to $350 a year and Betterment Digital to $250.

Crossing $25,000 adds unlimited 1-on-1 financial coaching sessions with advisors. Taxable accounts at that level also get tax-loss harvesting opportunities in Flex Funds that hold stocks. Clients with $500,000 or more at Fidelity may be eligible for a dedicated representative.

Fidelity Go fits investors under $25,000 who want no advisory fee, and investors above that line who want coaching sessions.

alternatives.heading: Acorns Subscription Plans and Round-Ups
alternatives.body:
Acorns charges a flat monthly subscription with no transaction fees: Bronze at $4, Silver at $8 and Gold at $12. Over a year, those plans cost $48, $96 and $144. Bronze includes an investment account with a diversified portfolio, Round-Ups spare-change investing, the Acorns Later retirement account, Acorns Earn bonus investments and learning courses.

Silver adds Real-Time Round-Ups, paycheck split, bonus investments matched up to 25% and live Q&As. It also lists a 1% IRA match on new contributions in the first year and a 3.59% APY on Emergency Savings (variable, as of September 22, 2026). Gold adds an investment account for kids with a 1% match, bonus investments matched up to 50%, a 3% IRA match on new first-year contributions and family tools.

A flat fee costs a different share of each balance. On $5,000, Bronze's $48 a year equals 0.96%, while Betterment's $60 a year equals 1.2%. On $30,000, Bronze's $48 is below Betterment's $75 at 0.25%.

Acorns checking, called Mighty Oak, lists a 2.33% APY as of September 22, 2026, no overdraft fees and 55,000+ fee-free ATMs in the AllPoint network. Acorns is not a bank; nbkc bank or Lincoln Savings Bank provide the banking, both members FDIC. Acorns also lists a Premium plan with a $10,000 life insurance policy and a will for eligible customers, with no price on its pricing page.

Acorns fits investors who want Round-Ups and an IRA match under one subscription. More picks are on the [Acorns alternatives](/alternatives/acorns/) page.

alternatives.heading: Ally Invest Robo Portfolios and the 30% Cash Buffer
alternatives.body:
Ally Invest Robo Portfolios open with $100 and come in two versions. The cash-enhanced portfolio charges no advisory fee and holds 30% as an interest-earning cash buffer at 3.20% a year, credited monthly. Ally says that cash buffer is not accessible like savings and is not FDIC insured.

The second version invests about 98% in the market for a 0.30% annual advisory fee, which is $3 per $1,000. About 2% stays in cash earning 3.20%. On $30,000, the fee is $90 a year, against $75 at Betterment's 0.25% rate.

Ally charges the fee within the first 10 days of each month based on the daily portfolio balance. ETF expense ratios are separate from the advisory fee. Personal Advice requires a $100,000 minimum, and SIPC coverage runs up to $500,000, including $250,000 for cash.

Ally Invest Robo Portfolios fits investors who want a $100 start and a choice between a $0 advisory fee with 30% in cash or 0.30% with about 98% invested.

alternatives.heading: M1 Platform Fee and Self-Directed Automation
alternatives.body:
M1 offers self-directed investing with automation and charges no commission, trading or management fees on self-directed brokerage accounts. A $3 monthly platform fee applies, which is $36 a year. M1 waives that fee for clients with more than $10,000 at M1.

On $30,000, M1's platform fee is waived, against $75 a year at Betterment's 0.25% rate. M1 accounts are self-directed, so the investor picks the holdings. Betterment's own self-directed accounts also trade stocks and ETFs with no commissions, and Betterment's management fee does not apply to them.

M1 lists a High-Yield Cash Account at 3.35% APY (variable, $100 minimum initial deposit). Cash is swept to partner banks eligible for FDIC insurance up to an aggregate of $4.75 million. Margin loans run 5.90% on accounts with at least $2,000 in eligible securities.

SIPC protection covers up to $500,000, and M1 reports more than $14 billion in client assets as of September 2026. M1 fits investors who want self-directed investing with automation and no management fee.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Betterment and each alternative leave some investors out, based on the published fees and minimums.

- Betterment fits poorly for balances under $24,000 with no recurring deposits of $200 a month, because the $5 monthly charge equals 1.2% a year on $5,000. Fidelity Go charges $0 in advisory fees below $25,000.
- Betterment Premium fits poorly for households under $100,000, its minimum. Betterment Digital at 0.25% has no such minimum.
- Schwab Intelligent Portfolios fits poorly for anyone starting with less than $5,000. Vanguard Digital Advisor and Ally take $100, and Fidelity Go starts investing at $10.
- Acorns fits poorly for very small balances, because Bronze costs $48 a year at any balance; on $1,000 that equals 4.8%. Fidelity Go charges no advisory fee at that size.
- The Ally cash-enhanced portfolio fits poorly for investors who want the whole balance invested, because 30% stays in a cash buffer that is not FDIC insured. Ally's 0.30% option invests about 98%.
- M1 fits poorly for investors who want the portfolio built for them, because its accounts are self-directed.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Betterment Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Each yearly cost figure on this page comes from a published fee, and any of these changes would move those figures:

- Betterment lowering or removing the $5 monthly charge below $24,000, or changing the $200 recurring-deposit trigger for the 0.25% rate.
- Wealthfront changing its 0.25% advisory fee.
- Schwab lowering its $5,000 minimum for Intelligent Portfolios.
- Vanguard changing the 90-day $0 advisory fee period or its approximation of about $15 to $16 per $10,000.
- Fidelity Go moving its $25,000 threshold or its 0.35% rate.
- Acorns changing its $4, $8 and $12 plan prices or the Silver and Gold IRA matches.
- Ally changing the 30% cash buffer, the 3.20% rate on it or the 0.30% fee.
- M1 changing the $10,000 waiver on its $3 platform fee.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Betterment Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Betterment fits investors who want automated investing with no minimum balance and a cash account, checking and retirement accounts at one company. The $5 monthly price applies from $0. Recurring deposits of $200 or more a month move the account to 0.25% before the balance reaches $24,000.

Betterment lists automated and self-directed investing, high-yield cash, traditional, Roth and Simplified Employee Pension (SEP) IRAs, crypto investing and checking. It also lists trusts, a Solo 401(k), 401(k) plans for businesses and custom portfolios. Checking has no overdraft fees and reimburses ATM fees and the Visa 1% foreign transaction fee, though checking does not earn APY.

Cash Reserve has no monthly management fee, a $10 minimum deposit for the base APY and an extra 0.75% for new clients with a qualifying deposit, for 4.25% through April 16, 2027. FDIC insurance runs through Program Banks up to $250,000 per depositor per bank, with a potential aggregate of $4 million, or $8 million for joint accounts. Checking is provided by nbkc bank, Member FDIC.

Above $1 million, Betterment's fee drops to 0.15% on the portion from $1 million to $2 million and 0.10% above $2 million, on both Digital and Premium. On $1.5 million in Digital, that is $2,500 on the first $1 million plus $750 on the next $500,000, or $3,250 a year. Premium costs 0.65% on the first $1 million, which is $1,300 a year on $200,000.

Betterment provides a free transfer specialist team, and a complimentary Licensed Concierge team for those moving $20,000 or more.

verdict:
Schwab Intelligent Portfolios charges no advisory fee from $5,000, and Fidelity Go charges none below $25,000. Wealthfront matches Betterment's 0.25% rate, and Vanguard Digital Advisor approximates about $15 to $16 a year per $10,000 in an all-index portfolio. Ally charges $0 or 0.30% depending on how much stays in cash.

Acorns charges $4 to $12 a month for Round-Ups and IRA matches, and M1 waives its $3 platform fee above $10,000 for self-directed investors. Betterment fits investors who want no minimum, a cash account, checking and IRAs at one company, with the 0.25% rate reachable through $200 a month in recurring deposits.

To narrow these Betterment alternatives, write down your invested balance and your monthly deposit, then read the fee for that balance in each row of the table above.

faqs.question: How much does Betterment cost?
faqs.answer: Betterment charges $5 per month for automated investing on balances of $0 to $24,000. The fee switches to 0.25% a year with recurring deposits of $200 or more a month, or at a $24,000 balance. Premium costs 0.65% a year on the first $1 million with a $100,000 household minimum. Fund fees are charged on top, and moving an investing account to another company costs $75.

faqs.question: Does Betterment have a minimum balance?
faqs.answer: No. Betterment's $5 per month automated investing price has no minimum balance, and no fee is charged when there is no balance. Betterment Premium requires a $100,000 minimum eligible investment balance per household, and Cash Reserve needs a $10 minimum deposit for the base APY.

faqs.question: Is Betterment FDIC insured?
faqs.answer: Betterment's investments are not FDIC insured and may lose value. Cash Reserve carries FDIC insurance through Program Banks up to $250,000 per depositor per bank, with a potential aggregate of $4 million, or $8 million for joint accounts. Betterment checking is provided by nbkc bank, Member FDIC, and insured up to $250,000 per depositor. Betterment Securities is a member of SIPC.

faqs.question: Is Betterment worth the fee?
faqs.answer: At $30,000, Betterment costs $75 a year, the same as Wealthfront and more than Schwab Intelligent Portfolios at $0 in advisory fees. Below $24,000 without $200 a month in recurring deposits, Betterment costs $60 a year, while Fidelity Go charges $0 under $25,000. For that fee, Betterment bundles checking, Cash Reserve, IRAs and self-directed trading with no commissions.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest robo-advisor?
faqs.answer: Among the eight services here, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios and the Ally cash-enhanced portfolio charge no advisory fee at any balance, and Fidelity Go charges none under $25,000. Schwab requires $5,000 to open, and Ally's cash-enhanced version holds 30% in a cash buffer. Fund expense ratios are charged on top and are set by each fund.

title: Ally Bank Alternatives Compared by Savings Rate and Fees
h1: Ally Bank Alternatives Compared by Savings Rate and Fees
metaDescription: Ally Bank alternatives compared: Capital One 360, Marcus, SoFi, Axos, Chase and Wells Fargo by savings rate, monthly fees and branch access.
intro:
Capital One 360, Marcus by Goldman Sachs, SoFi, Axos Bank, Chase Total Checking and Wells Fargo Everyday Checking are six Ally Bank alternatives for online savings and checking. They differ on the published savings annual percentage yield (APY), the monthly fee, and whether you get branches or an online-only account. At The Modern Wallet, we compared each provider's published rates and fees, and the sections below run the arithmetic on a $10,000 balance.

[Ally Bank](https://www.ally.com/bank/) lists its Savings account at 3.2% APY as of November 19, 2026, with no monthly maintenance fees and no minimum balance. Ally has no branches, and its phone line at 1-877-247-2559 is open 24/7. Ally Bank is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) member, and its lineup covers a Spending checking account, Savings, certificates of deposit (CDs), a Money Market account and individual retirement accounts (IRAs).

Marcus lists 3.50% APY on its Online Savings Account, and SoFi lists 3.30% APY for members with Eligible Direct Deposit. Chase and Wells Fargo charge $15 a month unless one waiver condition is met, while Ally, Capital One 360, Marcus and SoFi list $0 monthly fees. Listed automated teller machine (ATM) counts run from 14,000+ at Chase to 75,000+ no-fee ATMs at Ally.

For savings-only shortlists, see the [best high-yield savings accounts roundup](/roundup/best-high-yield-savings-accounts/). Business owners can start with the [best business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/), and parents can read the guide to [high-yield savings accounts for kids and teens](/guides/high-yield-savings-account-for-kids-and-teens/). The [Wealthfront alternatives](/alternatives/wealthfront/) page and the [comparison hub](/compare/) list more side-by-side breakdowns.
