chooseSection.heading: How to Choose an Ally Bank Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Four published numbers separate Ally Bank from the six alternatives in the table.

- Savings APY: Ally 3.2%, Marcus 3.50%, SoFi 3.30% with Eligible Direct Deposit, and Axos ONE up to 4.21% with conditions. Capital One's 360 Performance Savings APY is variable, and its page shows no figure as of November 20, 2026.
- Rate conditions: Ally and Capital One 360 Performance Savings list no minimum balance, and Marcus lists no minimum deposit. SoFi and Axos tie their higher rates to direct deposits or qualifying deposits.
- Monthly fees: Ally, Capital One 360, Marcus, SoFi and Axos ONE list no monthly maintenance fee. Chase Total Checking and Wells Fargo Everyday Checking list $15 a month.
- In-person access: Ally has no branches and accepts no cash by mail or at ATMs. Chase lists 5,000+ branches, and Capital One lists Capital One Cafes for in-person support.

The savings rate gap is simple to price. On a $10,000 balance, Ally's 3.2% APY works out to $320 a year before compounding. Marcus at 3.50% works out to $350, and SoFi at 3.30% works out to $330.

Every APY in the table is variable. The dollar figures illustrate the rates published in November 2026 and do not forecast future interest. Marcus pays 0.30 percentage points more than Ally, which is $30 a year on $10,000 and $300 a year on $100,000.

Checking fees can outweigh that gap. A $15 monthly fee at Chase or Wells Fargo costs $180 a year when no waiver applies. That $180 is six times the $30 yearly APY gap between Ally and Marcus on $10,000.

alternatives.heading: Capital One 360 Checking and Performance Savings
alternatives.body:
Capital One 360 pairs a checking account with no fees to open, keep or use and a savings account with a $0 monthly maintenance fee. 360 Checking lists no minimum balance, no overdraft fees, a no-fee debit card and Zelle. The overdraft choices are Auto-Decline, Free Savings Transfer and no-fee Overdraft.

The Capital One ATM network covers 70,000+ fee-free Capital One, MoneyPass and Allpoint ATMs, including select Target, Walgreens and CVS stores. Ally lists 75,000+ no-fee Allpoint and MoneyPass ATMs and reimburses up to $10 per statement cycle for fees at other ATMs. Capital One also lists Capital One Cafes for in-person support, and Ally has no branches.

360 Performance Savings has no minimum balance, and interest accrues daily and compounds monthly. Ally compounds interest daily. Capital One's 360 Performance Savings APY is variable and its page shows no figure as of November 20, 2026, so the Capital One row carries no figure to set against Ally's 3.2%.

One FDIC detail applies to Discover customers. Discover Bank accounts opened on or after May 18, 2025 count with Capital One deposit accounts for FDIC coverage.

Capital One 360 fits savers who want $0-fee checking and savings with the option of in-person help at a Capital One Cafe.

alternatives.heading: Marcus by Goldman Sachs Online Savings Rate
alternatives.body:
Marcus by Goldman Sachs lists its Online Savings Account at 3.50% APY as of November 20, 2026. The rate is variable, and maximum balance limits apply. Marcus lists no fees, no minimum deposit and no credit check.

On $10,000, 3.50% works out to $350 a year before compounding, against $320 at Ally's 3.2%. Marcus pays $30 more on that balance, and the Marcus page shows no checking account. Ally pairs its Savings account with a Spending account that has unlimited deposits and withdrawals, bill pay, Zelle, checks and a debit card.

Marcus lists same-day transfers of $100,000 or less to and from other banks, and its contact center is open 24/7. Ally lists standard or expedited transfers at $0. Marcus deposit products come from Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Salt Lake City Branch, Member FDIC.

A friend referral can earn both the referrer and a new-to-Marcus friend a 1.00% APY rate boost for 3 months. On $10,000, an extra 1.00% for 3 months adds about $25 before compounding.

Marcus fits savers who want a 3.50% savings rate with no deposit conditions and who keep checking at another bank.

alternatives.heading: SoFi Checking and Savings Direct Deposit Rates
alternatives.body:
SoFi Checking and Savings lists no account, service or maintenance fees and no minimum balance. The savings APY is 3.30% for members with Eligible Direct Deposit, variable and current as of 10/20/26. New members can reach up to 4.40% APY with a limited-time 1.10% APY Boost.

The SoFi APY Boost requires Eligible Direct Deposit or Qualifying Deposits, such as $5,000 in Qualifying Deposits every 31 days. On $10,000, 3.30% works out to $330 a year before compounding, $10 more than Ally's $320. The 4.40% figure is 3.30% plus the 1.10% boost, and SoFi calls that boost limited-time.

SoFi Overdraft Coverage requires at least $1,000 of Eligible Direct Deposits in a rolling 31 days. It covers a negative balance of up to $50 on debit card purchases only. Ally CoverDraft covers up to $100, or up to $250 after a qualifying direct deposit of at least $250 for two months in a row, and Ally never charges an overdraft fee.

SoFi lists 55,000+ Allpoint ATMs with no fee in network, and third-party fees may apply out of network. SoFi charges fees for outgoing wire transfers, Instant Transfers and global remittance transfers. Ally lists $20 for an outgoing domestic wire.

SoFi fits savers with Eligible Direct Deposit who want checking and savings in one account.

alternatives.heading: Axos ONE and Summit Savings Rate Conditions
alternatives.body:
Axos ONE bundles savings and checking with no monthly maintenance, opening or overdraft fees. The base APY is 0.00% on checking and up to 1.00% on savings. Boosted rates are 0.51% on checking and 4.21% on savings for the first $249,999.99, with 3.50% above that.

Axos ONE sets two ways to earn the boosted rates.

- Option 1: monthly direct deposits of at least $1,500 and an average daily checking balance of at least $1,500.
- Option 2: $5,000 of qualifying deposits and a $5,000 average daily balance.

The Axos arithmetic depends on meeting one option. On $10,000, 4.21% works out to $421 a year before compounding, $101 more than Ally's $320. At the base savings rate of up to 1.00%, the same $10,000 earns up to $100, which is $220 less than Ally.

On checking, 0.51% on a $1,500 balance pays $7.65 a year. Ally Spending pays 0.1% under $15,000, which is $1.50 a year on $1,500.

New Axos customers get a limited-time promotion that adds 0.79% on the first $49,999.99, for 5.00% total on that portion. On $10,000, 5.00% equals $500 over a year at that promotional rate. Axos ONE also lists early payday up to 2 days and expanded coverage up to $2.5 million under the Axos Insured deposit program.

Summit Savings lists up to 4.01% APY for up to 6 months, including a limited-time 0.26% APY boost for new customers. Summit lists no minimum balance for the APY, no monthly maintenance fees and no minimum initial deposit. Over six months, 4.01% on $10,000 works out to about $200.50 before compounding.

Axos ONE fits savers who meet Option 1 or Option 2.

alternatives.heading: Chase Total Checking Branches and Fee Waivers
alternatives.body:
Chase Total Checking charges a $15 Monthly Service Fee unless one of three conditions is met in the statement period.

- $500 or more in qualifying electronic deposits.
- A beginning-of-day balance of $1,500 or more.
- An average beginning-day balance of $5,000 or more in this account or with linked qualifying personal deposits or investments.

Missing every Chase waiver costs $15 a month, or $180 a year. Ally Spending charges no monthly maintenance fee and has no minimum balance. Chase lists 14,000+ ATMs and 5,000+ branches, while Ally has no branches and lists 75,000+ no-fee ATMs.

Chase charges no overdraft fee when an account is overdrawn by $50 or less at the end of the business day, or brought to $50 or less by the next business day. Ally never charges an overdraft fee and offers opt-in CoverDraft at no charge. The Chase Total Checking terms list fees, waivers, ATMs and branches with no interest rate, while Ally Spending pays 0.1% APY under $15,000 and 0.25% at $15,000 or more.

Chase Total Checking fits customers who want branch access and meet one of the three fee waivers.

alternatives.heading: Wells Fargo Everyday Checking Fees and ATM Costs
alternatives.body:
Wells Fargo Everyday Checking charges a $15 monthly service fee unless one of five conditions is met.

- A $1,500 minimum daily balance.
- $500 or more in qualifying electronic deposits.
- A primary owner aged 17 to 24.
- $5,000 or more in qualifying deposit and/or investment balances.
- A qualifying military direct deposit through the Worldwide Military Banking program.

Wells Fargo charges $0 per withdrawal at Wells Fargo ATMs and $3 per withdrawal at non-Wells Fargo ATMs in the U.S. Four out-of-network withdrawals a month cost $12, or $144 a year. Outside the U.S., Wells Fargo charges $5 per withdrawal plus operator fees, while Ally lists international transactions at up to 1%.

Ally lists 75,000+ no-fee ATMs and reimburses up to $10 per statement cycle for fees at other ATMs nationwide. Wells Fargo notes that other fees may apply for overdraft, wires and optional services. Ally lists $20 for an outgoing domestic wire and never charges an overdraft fee.

Wells Fargo Everyday Checking fits primary owners aged 17 to 24 and customers who meet another waiver and use Wells Fargo ATMs.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Ally Bank and each alternative set a limit that rules some savers out, and each limit has an option elsewhere in the table.

- Savers who deposit cash fit poorly with Ally, which accepts no cash by mail or at ATMs (Ally lists cash deposits at Walmart through its app). Chase lists 5,000+ branches, and Capital One lists Capital One Cafes for in-person support.
- Ally Savings fits poorly for frequent withdrawals. Ally limits Savings and Money Market withdrawals to 10 per statement cycle in total, and it may close accounts that exceed the limit more than occasionally. The Ally Spending account has unlimited deposits and withdrawals.
- Marcus fits poorly for anyone who wants checking and savings at one provider, since the Marcus page shows no checking account. Ally, Capital One 360, SoFi and Axos ONE list both.
- SoFi's 3.30% rate fits poorly for savers without Eligible Direct Deposit. Marcus lists 3.50% and Ally lists 3.2% with no direct deposit condition.
- Axos ONE fits poorly for savers who meet neither Option 1 nor Option 2, because savings then earns a base APY of up to 1.00%. Axos Summit Savings lists no minimum balance for its APY.
- Chase Total Checking and Wells Fargo Everyday Checking fit poorly for anyone who meets no waiver, at $180 a year in fees. Ally Spending, Capital One 360 Checking and SoFi list no monthly maintenance fee.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Ally Bank Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Our answer would shift if any of these published terms moved.

- Ally raising its 3.2% savings APY to 3.50% or higher, which would close the gap with Marcus.
- Capital One displaying a numeric 360 Performance Savings APY that can be set against Ally's 3.2%.
- SoFi removing the Eligible Direct Deposit condition from its 3.30% savings rate.
- Axos lowering the $1,500 or $5,000 thresholds behind its 4.21% savings rate.
- Chase or Wells Fargo dropping the $15 monthly fee or changing its waiver conditions.
- Ally changing its 10-withdrawal limit or starting to accept cash deposits.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Ally Bank Is the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Ally Bank fits savers who want savings, checking, CDs and a money market account at one online bank with no monthly maintenance fees. Interest compounds daily on Ally accounts. Ally lists no minimum opening deposit on Savings or Spending.

The Ally Spending account carries no overdraft fees and no minimum balance. CoverDraft, an opt-in feature, covers overdrafts up to $100 at no charge, rising to $250 after a qualifying direct deposit of at least $250 for two months in a row. CoverDraft is typically available 30 days after a total of $100 is deposited.

Ally Savings adds savings buckets and boosters. Boosters include recurring transfers and round ups, which transfer money once at least $5 accrues, with each transfer between $5 and $20. Ally states that people who actively use its smart savings tools grew total savings 2x more on average in the first 12 months.

The Ally Money Market Account also pays 3.2% APY and adds a debit card, checks and eCheck Deposit by phone photo. Ally CDs need no minimum deposit, and CD APYs are fixed for the term while the 3.2% Savings APY is variable. On $10,000, the 2.9% No Penalty CD works out to $290 over a year, $30 less than the $320 Savings pays at 3.2%.

The No Penalty CD allows withdrawing the full balance after the first six days with no penalty. The Raise Your Rate CD at 3% APY allows one rate increase over the 2-year term or two over the 4-year term. Ally also lists a Ten Day Best Rate Guarantee and automatic renewal on its CDs.

verdict:
Ally Bank fits savers who want five deposit product lines at one online bank, $0 monthly fees, no overdraft fees and 75,000+ no-fee ATMs. Marcus lists a higher savings APY at 3.50% with no deposit conditions and shows no checking account. SoFi and Axos ONE publish higher rates tied to direct deposits or balance tests.

Capital One 360 adds Capital One Cafes for in-person support at $0 monthly fees. Chase Total Checking and Wells Fargo Everyday Checking add branch access at $15 a month unless a waiver is met.

To pick among these Ally Bank alternatives, write down the monthly direct deposit amount and average balance you expect, then match them to the rate conditions and fee waivers in the table above.

faqs.question: Is Ally Bank FDIC insured?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ally Bank is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) member, and its deposit products include Spending, Savings, Money Market, CDs and IRAs. Ally has no branches, and its phone line at 1-877-247-2559 is open 24/7.

faqs.question: Does Ally Bank charge monthly fees?
faqs.answer: No. Ally lists no monthly maintenance fees and no minimum balance requirements on its Savings, Money Market and Spending accounts. Ally does list service fees: $15 for expedited debit card delivery, $20 for an outgoing domestic wire, $15 for a stop payment, $14.95 for overnight bill pay, $9.95 for same-day bill pay and up to 1% on international transactions.

faqs.question: What is Ally Bank's savings APY?
faqs.answer: Ally Bank lists 3.2% APY on its Savings account as of November 19, 2026. The rate is variable, and interest compounds daily. On $10,000, 3.2% works out to $320 a year before compounding, against $350 at Marcus's 3.50%.

faqs.question: Does Ally Bank have ATMs?
faqs.answer: Ally Bank customers get no-fee withdrawals at 75,000+ Allpoint and MoneyPass ATMs. Ally reimburses up to $10 per statement cycle for fees at other ATMs nationwide. Ally accepts no cash deposits at ATMs or by mail.

faqs.question: Does Ally Bank have overdraft fees?
faqs.answer: No. Ally never charges an overdraft fee on its Spending account. Opt-in CoverDraft covers overdrafts up to $100 at no charge, or up to $250 after a qualifying direct deposit of at least $250 for two months in a row.

related.label: High-yield savings accounts for kids and teens
